Sports.title: Antonelli’s coronation, Mexico’s optional turn one and more Mexican GP talking points | Formula 1
Sports.content:
The world championship outcome may be a foregone conclusion but there are plenty of other talking points of note at this weekend’s Mexican Grand Prix.

All over bar the shouting

There could hardly be less doubt over the destination of this year’s world drivers’ championship. Yes, theoretically there are still three drivers in the hunt, but the two who aren’t Andrea Kimi Antonelli realistically need him not to score in the next four consecutive races to still be in with a shot come the final round.

On top of that, consider that at least one of the remaining rounds might not go ahead anyway. In which case even this flimsy conjecture is moot, and the championship is already Antonelli’s.

But if, as seems almost certain, he does win the title this weekend, what a venue to do it at. If the remodelled Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez has one thing going for it, it’s the joyous theatre of F1 fever which greets drivers in the stadium at the end of the race.

Optional turn one

The opening trio of corners on the Mexico City track has been a trouble spot since Hermann Tilke’s designers reworked the layout for the race’s return in 2015. The tight corner configuration and generous run-off area make it easy for drivers to abuse track limits at this point on the track.

Last year’s start was a particularly egregious example as multiple drivers arguably benefitted from cutting the corner. Max Verstappen’s approach to it gave every indication he never intended to stay within the track’s boundaries.

Will race control take note and put stricter measures in place? There was little sign this was a priority in Austin last weekend, where track limits have long been a problem.

Debutants Slater and Mini join the rookies

At least two drivers will make their debuts in an F1 practice session this weekend. Audi’s promising rookie Freddie Slater, who finished second in Formula 3 this year, will take over Gabriel Bortoleto’s car for first practice. Alpine’s Gabriele Mini will be in Franco Colapinto’s car.

Several of the regular practice session drivers will also appear: Frederik Vesti at Mercedes, Luke Browning at Williams and Ryo Hirakawa at Haas. Some teams are yet to confirm their plans.

Mexico versus Lawson

Liam Lawson was at the centre of a bizarre incident last year when he had the misfortune to encounter two marshals on track. Incredibly, Mexico’s automobile club accused the blameless driver of being responsible for the oversight.

The FIA later made it clear Lawson had done nothing wrong. Hopefully there is no repeat of either administrative slip-up this year.

Perez hits 300

Last year’s Mexican Grand Prix was the first without a home driver since the event returned to the calendar. But Sergio Perez is back on the grid this year and will mark his 300th start in front of his home crowd.

Expect the usual huge cheers for the Guadalajaran. However the hope of a points finish looks as remote as ever. Indeed, the combination of high cooling demands and several heavy braking points could aggravate one of Cadillac’s most obvious weaknesses.

With Andrea Kimi Antonelli poised to win the world championship this weekend, has Formula 1’s ruined season diminished his inevitable triumph? Rick disagrees:

I agree with the disappointing season but I don’t think it takes away from soon to be Antonelli’s championship season. In my almost 50 years of watching F1 there have been many unusual situations and this season will just be added to that list.

I find the biggest problem is that the current ownership knows that they can bring in more casual watchers by reducing true racing and making the spectacle more “entertaining” which in turn means more profit. Will that change? I doubt it because to the owners, it’s about the show and how much revenue it generates, not about racing.

I’ve lived in six countries, most of my life in the USA, and I can say with confidence that greed is the driving force in the country. I’m absolutely not against striving for something, working hard and making huge amounts of money. The problem is when you sacrifice the quality of your life for the desire to make more. In my opinion, that attitude is what drives F1 now and until it changes, I doubt we will see true racing.

Rick Gomez (@Rgomez13)

Sports.title: Stats: Russell scored as many points as Hulkenberg in last three rounds | 2026 United States GP stats and facts
Sports.content:
Andrea Kimi Antonelli is on the verge of sealing a historic championship triumph following his victory in the United States Grand Prix.

George Russell was Mercedes’ most recent race-winner going into Austin, and this was Antonelli’s first win in over a month. But Russell’s fading championship challenge has collapsed entirely over the last three rounds.

The rot set in with his retirement in Malaysia, which not only left him point-less but prompted a grid penalty in Singapore. He compounded matters there by crashing out of the sprint race while leading.

The upshot is, with only an eighth and a ninth place to count from his last three grand prix weekends, Russell has added just six points to his tally in that time. He has been out-scored by eight of his rivals, including Racing Bulls driver Liam Lawson, who picked up three times as many points as Russell over the period.

Underlining just how badly the last three rounds have gone for Russell, his haul of six points matches that of Nico Hulkenberg, who lies 14th in the championship standings.

Antonelli’s ninth career victory last weekend means he has now won more grands prix than his team mate. He has drawn level with rivals Charles Leclerc and Oscar Piastri – plus Piastri’s manager, Mark Webber.

Thanks to Antonelli’s success this year, and Piastri’s failure to win since last year’s Dutch Grand Prix, Italian drivers now have as many grand prix wins as Australians. Antonelli claimed the 52nd grand prix win for an Italian driver, putting the two nations level in seventh place on the all-time list.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

Antonelli also scored his seventh pole position, giving him as many as Jacques Laffite. But he missed out on the fastest lap, which Leclerc scored for the second race in a row. It is Leclerc’s 15th fastest lap, matching his Ferrari predecessors Felipe Massa and Clay Regazzoni, plus three-times world champion Jackie Stewart.

Isack Hadjar equalled the best qualifying position of his career with third place. He previously achieved this in the Australian Grand Prix earlier this year.

Unusually, both Red Bull drivers finished lower than they started. However their recent upswing in form continued and they look increasingly likely to avoid finishing outside the top three in the championship for the first time since 2015. They out-scored McLaren for the fifth round in a row, have drawn level with them on 355 points, and are classified ahead of them in third place by dint of their higher finishing positions in races.

However third place for Max Verstappen means he is no longer a championship contender for the first time in almost six years. The last race Verstappen competed in which he could not take the title was the 2020 season finale at Yas Marina. He dropped out of contention for that year’s championship four rounds earlier at Imola.

Finally, Gabriel Bortoleto set a new record for the largest grid drop penalty ever issued to an F1 driver. He collected a total grid drop of 80 places after Audi replaced multiple parts of his power unit during the weekend. As he qualified 13th and started 21st, he only served 10% of the penalty. The record was previously held by Jenson Button, who had a 70-place grid penalty at the 2015 Mexican Grand Prix.

Sports.title: Has Boxing Made Waiting More Profitable Than Fighting?
Sports.content:
A fighter collects the biggest paycheck of his life, and boxing pays for it for the next twelve months. The money lands in the bank, the entourage celebrates, and the division goes on ice. Once an inflated check becomes the baseline, regular title defenses suddenly look like bad investments.

Oscar De La Hoya called out this trend, pointing out that too many top fighters now sit around waiting for what he termed the ultimate purse. He hit on an uncomfortable reality. A packed stadium show might generate headlines for forty-eight hours, but it leaves behind a barren schedule when the headliner disappears until another lottery ticket surfaces.

Taking a massive purse makes plenty of personal sense. A fighter walks away with security, leverage, and a shiny target on his back. Taking a dangerous fight for ordinary money suddenly looks foolish to his handlers. A loss wrecks his market value. A rough night hurts his bargaining position. Inactivity turns into the safest play on the board.

The trouble starts when every recognized name adopts that same corporate logic. Legitimate contenders get bypassed because they represent too much risk for the return. Solid, respectable paydays get treated like personal insults. The only bout worth taking is one against an opponent who will not push back.

Fighters forget that extraordinary money usually comes from extraordinary circumstances. A blood feud, an undisputed clash, or an eager backer with deep pockets creates an artificial economy that standard pay-per-view cards cannot duplicate. When fighters confuse a unique financial windfall with their permanent market rate, every future negotiation stalls before anyone even signs a contract.

Nobody argues that athletes in a brutal trade should risk their health for pocket change. Fighters take real physical damage, and securing their future is the goal of the sport. Promoters, networks, and sanctioning bodies also share blame for dragging out talks.

Yet the sport still suffers the damage. Belts sit idle, contenders get frozen out, and divisions grind to a halt. When the star finally agrees to return, fans get fed an overmatched tune-up disguised as a necessary prelude to the meaningful bout somewhere down the road.

Supporters get tired of following mandatory rotations, press conference callouts, and endless contract leaks that lead nowhere. Hardcore fans want action, not accounting lessons. When staying active requires another state-funded fortune to lure a champion out of his living room, people simply tune out.

High pay does not demand total inactivity. Naoya Inoue proved that by stepping into the ring four times in 2025. He proved that an elite attraction can handle a relentless schedule without sitting out a year between appearances.

Massive purses make big events happen, but they poison the water when their main legacy is an impossible asking price and a dormant champion. Boxing needs its stars to earn well, but the sport only survives when fighters actually fight. If the business continues rewarding long absences, fans will find another sport to follow.

Sports.title: Brandon Adams Gives Golden Boy Another Vergil Ortiz Option
Sports.content:
Golden Boy Promotions secured a credible future option for Vergil Ortiz Jr. by signing Brandon Adams, yet the transaction arrives too late to upgrade the December 5th DAZN PPV card. Keith Thurman holds that spot, making Adams an appealing option, but one that arrives at an inconvenient moment for fans.

Thurman’s recognizable past moves the promotional needle for pay-per-view, but his recent ring form does not justify top billing against an elite puncher in his prime. After getting battered and stopped in six rounds by Sebastian Fundora, Thurman looks completely spent at the world level. He has fought sparingly over the last several years, his timing is faded, and putting him in front of Vergil Ortiz Jr. feels more like an orchestrated cash grab than a legitimate sporting contest.

Adams would have provided a much harder night of work. He is active, possesses real grit, and holds two genuine victories over Serhii Bohachuk, including the unanimous decision in their rematch. That type of form provides actual resistance. Adams would force Ortiz to think, work on the inside, and deal with physical pressure.

Instead, paying viewers are asked to buy a legacy name whose best days happened nearly a decade ago at welterweight. Thurman likely tries to survive on movement early, but once Ortiz closes the distance and starts digging to the body, it probably turns one-sided in a hurry. It makes sense for Golden Boy money-wise, but it shortchanges anyone hoping to see Ortiz tested inside the ropes.

As for Adams, he cannot afford to let another half year slip away while Golden Boy waits on the aftermath of Ortiz Jr. versus Thurman. Having him sit on a shelf neutralizes the value of that September 2025 win over Bohachuk. Golden Boy needs to treat Adams as an active weapon rather than a back pocket backup plan.

Sports.title: Robert Garcia Demanded Naoya Inoue Contract, And He Was Right
Sports.content:
Hideyuki Ohashi wants everyone to know who handles the business. At Wednesday’s press conference in Tokyo, Naoya Inoue’s promoter made a point of lecturing Robert Garcia on proper boxing etiquette, even though Jesse “Bam” Rodriguez’s team just conceded to Inoue’s preferred schedule.

Rodriguez gave up an interim bout to make the dates work, yet Garcia gets scolded simply for requesting the actual paperwork.

“That’s not how it works. He’s mistaken,” Ohashi declared. While he shared positive updates regarding a March 2027 clash, he stopped short of announcing a finalized deal.

The friction traces back to Rodriguez’s preparation. Garcia initially wanted another bantamweight outing before jumping up to challenge Inoue. Inoue’s camp shut that idea down completely, telling Rodriguez to take March or watch the opportunity vanish.

Giving in was a major concession. That extra fight was central to Garcia’s readiness plan, but dropping it kept the Inoue clash alive. Garcia and promoter Eddie Hearn told BoxingScene they were ready to accept those terms, which prompted Garcia’s blunt demand: “Send the fucking contract.” The wording was colorful, but the expectation was clear.

Responding to Garcia’s contract demand, Ohashi dismissed the trainer-manager’s involvement, BoxingScene reported.

“He clearly doesn’t know how this goes,” Ohashi said, noting that talks belong at the promoter level rather than with the trainer.

Except Garcia manages Rodriguez too. Calling him just the trainer ignores the managerial role that gives him every right to review the contract. Ohashi might prefer dealing exclusively with Hearn, but Garcia has every reason to verify the financial terms after revamping his fighter’s calendar.

Inoue had cranked up the heat by declaring he was tired of waiting and ready to jump to featherweight. That left Rodriguez with a stark choice: protect the prep timeline and forfeit the bout, or agree to March and keep talking.

Rodriguez’s team gave Inoue the timeline he wanted. Now, the rest of the business must follow.

“Negotiations for Inoue’s next fight are moving forward, step by step. Everything is going well,” Ohashi noted, asking fans to look forward to March.

Inoue’s U.S. manager, John Lewis, also confirmed to Mike Coppinger that discussions with Matchroom are active. Still, neither side has confirmed signed financial terms. Agreeing on a date is only half the battle, and Rodriguez’s side must see what is actually written on the dotted line.

Ohashi’s optimism is great to hear, but brushing off Garcia falls flat. Rodriguez already gave up the tune-up fight; asking to see the contract is simply common sense.

Sports.title: Amanda Serrano Deserves Farewell Despite Weak Skye Falzon Matchup
Sports.content:
Amanda Serrano’s sendoff against Skye Falzon relies on nostalgia rather than pure sporting drama. Falzon brings regional hardware and a top ranking, yet lacks proven elite credentials. What we get is a routine title defense tied to a historic milestone, an arrangement Serrano has fully earned.

Serrano wraps up her legendary run on January 9 in San Juan, Puerto Rico, streaming live on DAZN. Holding belts across seven divisions, ruling undisputed at featherweight, and enduring three grueling battles with Katie Taylor means she has nothing left to prove. Still, every fight card deserves an honest look for what it actually presents.

You can understand the business calculation from Serrano’s camp: after twenty years, seven divisions, and the physical toll of three wars with Taylor, the desire to cash a final check without risking a bad knockout or a tainted scorecard makes self-preservation sense. But for fans who actually value real drama over a victory lap, it feels empty. Ending on a layup preserves the record, but it rarely produces the kind of memorable final high note people talk about years down the road.

Falzon sports a 12-2 record with seven stoppages, holding the WBA Asia and Oceania featherweight belts. Ranked fourth by the WBA, her paperwork checks out, yet those regional honors offer very little reason to expect a competitive scrap.

Her most recent outing saw her cruise past Monika Singh on September 11 with three matching 99-91 cards. Her only losses came early, dropping bouts to Sarah Watt in December 2021 and Pam McClelland in July 2022. She brings decent momentum, but regional dominance leaves one massive question looming over the ring: what happens once Serrano starts connecting?

That gap exposes the promotion’s biggest flaw. Sanctioning bodies provide official stamps, not guaranteed entertainment. Falzon has the numbers, but nothing suggests she can truly trouble the champ.

Nobody can fault Falzon for taking the call. Any fighter chasing a world crown would be crazy to turn down a golden ticket just because critics consider them outgunned.

“One last fight. One last walk. One final chapter,” Serrano posted on X. “Boxing has given me everything. It’s taken me around the world, allowed me to chase dreams I once thought were impossible, and given me the opportunity to inspire the next generation of fighters.”

That said, nothing is completely guaranteed inside the ropes. Serrano had to grind out a close majority decision over Lucrecia Manzur during her last defense. That showing proves that any slight dip in sharpness matters, even against an opponent with a lighter record.

At its core, the main attraction remains untouched. Puerto Rico gets to salute its greatest warrior. That moment means something, so there is no reason to pretend Falzon is a monster test. Serrano gets her well-earned homecoming, while supporters get an honest look at the match in front of them.

Sports.title: Keyshawn Davis Ducks $6 Million Question After Richardson Hitchins Says Fight Is Off
Sports.content:
Keyshawn Davis fired back against claims that he priced himself out of facing Richardson Hitchins, yet his heated response sidestepped the actual financial dispute. Davis stated he signed a bout contract back in August and insists Hitchins is the opponent he targets next. He never touched the alleged $6 million purse demand that Hitchins claimed blew up the deal.

Hitchins ignited the dispute on October 23, declaring the contest dead across social media while revealing the financial rift:

“Keyshawn Out Priced himself to fight me Like i said i been agreed to the fight going on 2 months i was wondering what was the hold up but He was asking for 6ms to fight me And mind you boy never even made more than a M in boxing #FIGHTOFF son a clown.”

Taking to social media, Davis focused heavily on personal bravery, flashing his Olympic pedigree to shut down talk that he backs down from rivals. That approach silences people questioning his heart. It does nothing to explain how two fighters calling each other out still managed to stall negotiations.

“Back in August, before he even started doing the interviews, I DM’d him saying, ‘The ink is dry. Did you sign your contract?’ He said, ‘Business will get handled soon.’ … Now he’s saying I overpriced myself. So he never got back with me that he signed,” Davis stated.

That reported interaction gives Davis his firmest talking point. If accurate, he told Hitchins his paperwork was locked down well before this public spat erupted, establishing a distinct timeline that challenges the opposing narrative.

The mystery sits inside whatever document he inked. Davis omitted the purse figures, skipped any special clauses, and avoided confirming if Hitchins held matching conditions. Putting ink to paper does not prove the final terms worked for both camps.

Davis shifted quickly from quoting direct messages to guessing at his his rival’s status. He assumed Hitchins probably avoided signing altogether, claiming that explained sudden talk about Brian Norman. The gap in knowledge counts. Davis can vouch for his own side of the table; he cannot verify the paperwork across the divide.

Hitchins brought up an exorbitant asking price, highlighting that Davis never collected a $ 1 million purse in his career. Davis countered with his readiness to trade punches. Both boxers can crave the contest while remaining completely split on compensation. Neither has established the pay-per-view drawing power required to justify an eight-figure event budget.

Davis has every right to secure his worth. Silencing accusations that excessive demands derailed the bout requires clear numbers: his requested purse, the promoter counteroffer, and the actual status of that proposal. A medal collection cannot clarify a balance sheet.

The talk surrounding Devin Haney clearly touched a nerve. Davis brought up Haney multiple times, batting away claims of fear while refusing to detail the actual business negotiations. Running into another collapsed deal gives detractors more ammunition, and repeating how fearless he feels will not convince skeptics.

“I want my next fight to be you. I don’t want nobody else,” Davis told Hitchins directly.

He told fans to flood the comment sections and prod his rival into accepting the contest. Shifting the heat onto an opponent plays well to an audience, yet it expects spectators to assign blame without seeing a single page of the paperwork.

Davis gave the boxing world a specific claim to chase by pointing to an August signature. The real challenge comes down to whether those terms back up his stance on the purse. Until he addresses the numbers behind that signature, he delivers pure theatrical heat without resolving the financial facts.

Sports.title: Andy Cruz Loses His Zero, Keeps His Problem
Sports.content:
Andy Cruz’s first professional defeat did little to boost his appeal to lightweight’s marquee names. Raymond Muratalla edged him in a grueling encounter that reinforced how dangerous Cruz remains. He surrendered his spotless record, yet none of the elite skill that makes him a nightmare opponent disappeared.

Cruz still demands top-tier competition. “William Zepeda. I’m coming for you,” he told reporters, singling out the WBC champion. Calling out the division’s best is simple enough. Persuading a champion to share a ring with him when safer, lucrative options exist is the real hurdle.

Muratalla earned respect for meeting Cruz head-on to retain his IBF belt. He brought steady pressure, landed big shots, and took home a majority decision. The scorecards of 114–114, 116–112, and 118–110 painted wildly divergent pictures of the bout. The Ring’s post-fight analysis favored Muratalla’s aggression while raising eyebrows at the wide 118–110 total.

The outcome proved Cruz could be outpointed at championship level. It offered zero comfort to rivals expecting an easy night. Muratalla worked relentlessly for all 12 rounds against a challenger who kept landing sharp counters. The loss revealed technical adjustments Cruz must make, yet his durability and ring IQ stayed intact.

Cruz answered in July by halting Abraham Montoya inside three rounds. That stoppage lifted his record to 7–1 with four knockouts, keeping his name in the mix. Steamrolling Montoya could not erase the tactical questions from the Muratalla clash. Facing another elite technician will reveal much more.

Landing that test remains the obstacle. Muratalla vacated his 135-pound strap to chase opportunities above, joined by Shakur Stevenson, who also left the division behind. Their exits put Zepeda and Abdullah Mason atop The Ring’s lightweight rankings, keeping Cruz hovering in the contender pack.

Mason recently floated Zepeda and Joe Cordina as potential targets. A clash with Zepeda brings a unification, while Cordina offers a credible defense. Cruz sat completely outside those discussions, despite loudly hunting Zepeda himself. That reality highlights his dilemma. Rival champions are not necessarily running scared, but they are looking elsewhere.

Cruz risks watching this cycle repeat. Elite fighters can chase unification paydays or fan-friendly matchups while he bides his time. Technical wizardry gives him an edge in any ring, but skill alone provides little financial incentive for rivals to take the risk.

The IBF’s mandate ordering Cruz to fight Artur Subkhankulov for the vacant lightweight crown provides an answer. Grabbing that strap would hand Cruz real leverage, giving unifications a genuine prize to dangle.

Even then, deals require willing partners. Cruz understands the gap between deserving a shot and securing one. His immediate test is capturing the title. Finding out if holding gold finally forces the division’s biggest stars to answer his call comes next.

Sports.title: O’Shaquie Foster Shows His Brilliance Against Emanuel Navarrete
Sports.content:
San Antonio, Texas – O’Shaquie “Ice Water” Foster demonstrated his technical boxing skills Saturday night by boxing brilliantly to defeat Emanuel “Vaquero” Navarrete by unanimous decision (115-111, 118-108×2). He outpointed him by putting on a masterclass. He was offensively sharp and defensively elusive.

Scoring a pair of knockdowns in the twelfth round and holding him to career lows in both total punches landed (99) and connect rate (18.8 %), Vaquero struggled offensively, not being able to land anything of significance, finding it difficult to find the target all night. His connect rate was anemic, landing in the single digits for 8 of the 12 rounds (Compubox).

With the win Foster (26-3, 12 KOs) captured the vacant Ring Magazine super featherweight championship and unified the WBO, IBF, and WBC titles. He now becomes the frontrunner for the fighter of the year award, having earned victories over Raymond Ford and Navarrete (40-3- 1, 33 KOs).

After the win, Foster told the media at the post-fight scrum, “I feel like it was a great performance. I finished strong man. I put him down twice at the end. I feel like there was a lot of people raving saying that I didn’t have no power and that I wasn’t going to be able to keep him off of me. I feel like I showed them tonight that I’m an all-around fighter.”

Many boxing experts believed this fight to be a 50-50 fight where either fighter could have come out victorious. O’Shaquie proved Saturday he is an elite fighter, having defeated another top fighter.

Since having lost controversially to Robson Conceicao in July of 2024, he’s showed significant improvement since then. Earning his revenge in the rematch against Conceicao, then defeating Stephen Fulton convincingly, followed by his most recent performances against Ford and Navarrete.

Vasiliy Lomachenko seems poised to come out of retirement and make an undisputed run in the 130-pound division, stating this is his normal weight and that he wants to become undisputed.

Foster has his eyes set on becoming undisputed champion and made it known to the media that this is his immediate goal and does not want to deviate from this by entertaining a fight with Shakur Stevenson or Lomachenko; for now, he wants to become undisputed.

The other divisional titleholder is WBA super featherweight champion Anthony Cacace, who is set to defend his title next against Nick Ball on December 19. O’Shaquie has every intent of pursuing a fight against the winner.

He did say he would be willing to fight Lomachenko afterwards, “I want Loma to get a tune-up fight or something cuz when I beat him I don’t want any excuses, man. He been retired.” With the return of Loma and Foster on the verge of becoming undisputed, it’s becoming one of the must-watch divisions.

Sports.title: Keith Thurman Can’t Talk Away The Fundora Loss
Sports.content:
Keith Thurman’s dismissal of Sebastian Fundora’s power makes his own performance harder to explain. If the punches were only “medium,” as Thurman insists, the unanswered question is why he couldn’t produce enough offense to keep the referee out of their fight.

“Medium. Medium, bro,” Thurman said to Brian Custer. “Like, I mean, come on. He never knocked me down.” Thurman’s defense of his performance rests heavily on that distinction: Fundora stopped him, but never put him on the floor.

Thurman rejected Fundora’s comment, relayed by Brian, that the referee had saved him from further punishment. He said a second-round counter pushed him downward because of Fundora’s height, rather than buckling his legs, and maintained that he could handle the punches.

“I’ve been in the ring with a lot of punchers, you know? I mean, at welterweight, Manny Pacquiao, Danny Garcia,” Thurman said. “It was medium. I could take that all day.”

That comparison draws on Thurman’s championship past, but his experience against established punchers cannot settle whether he was defending himself effectively against Fundora. His own description of the fight supplies a more revealing explanation than the power rating.

Thurman said Fundora’s height and reach were more difficult to deal with than he expected. Tall sparring partners had not fully prepared him for the distance he encountered, and he was still adjusting when the referee intervened.

Fundora did not need every punch to hurt Thurman badly if his reach and output kept Thurman occupied with protecting himself.

Thurman wanted more time, saying he had moved toward the middle of the ring and was beginning to feel comfortable defensively. He believed the decision should have remained with him and his corner.

“I just wish the ref would have used his eyes a little bit more and let me and my team make the decision, man,” Thurman said. “Like, if we get into the eighth round and it’s not getting any better, so be it. But I was determined to take the young man’s punches. It wasn’t really my night. My hands were not going.”

Thurman weakens his own argument by admitting he wasn’t throwing back. Being able to take Fundora’s punches wasn’t enough. He needed to answer them, and the referee didn’t have to wait for a knockdown to intervene.

Thurman also blamed an awkward weight cut and acknowledged a poor performance. Those explanations might account for his struggles, but they don’t explain why he believes more rounds would have changed anything.

Thurman had more to say when he discussed Fundora’s height, reach, and punch output. He admitted he couldn’t get comfortable against them. Calling Fundora’s power “medium” does nothing to explain why he couldn’t get past those advantages and land his own shots.

That version of the Fundora loss gives Golden Boy and DAZN something to sell: Thurman was still adjusting, his chin held up, and the referee denied him a chance to turn things around. It makes Ortiz sound like he’s facing a dangerous veteran whose right hand could punish a mistake. The harder sell is explaining how Thurman will land that punch after admitting he couldn’t get his offense going against Fundora.

Ghana News.title: The West pushing Africa back into debt abyss – Putin
Ghana News.content:
Russian President Vladimir Putin has accused Western countries of using debt, economic sanctions and trade restrictions to maintain influence over Africa, warning that harsh financing conditions could undermine the continent’s development.

Speaking at the third Russia-Africa Summit in Moscow on Wednesday, October 28, Mr Putin accused Western powers of pressuring African countries into financial arrangements that could divert resources from development priorities to debt repayment.

Delegations from 48 African countries are participating in the two-day summit, which runs from October 28 to 29, with discussions covering trade, investment, security, agriculture, technology and other areas of cooperation.

Mr Putin placed debt sustainability, industrialisation and economic sovereignty at the centre of his address, arguing that African countries needed greater control over their economic decisions and natural resources.

He said some Western countries were imposing unfavourable conditions on African nations seeking financial assistance, leaving them with obligations that could constrain their development plans.

“When they managed to enrich themselves at the expense of others, they are resorting to things as illegitimate sanctions, tariff wars, blackmail, interference in the domestic affairs of others. They are also trying to run the Africans back into the debt abyss.

“They are trying to impose resources on them, but on terrible terms, which are tantamount to robbery. And the African countries have to repay these debts to the detriment of developmental plans,” he said.

The Russian president also criticised the use of tariffs, sanctions and other forms of economic pressure, arguing that such measures were being deployed to preserve external influence over African economies.

Putin calls for increased intra-African trade

Mr Putin highlighted what he described as limited industrial development and low levels of trade among African countries as major obstacles to the continent’s economic independence.

He said manufacturing value addition in Africa remained below 2 per cent, while only about 15 per cent of the continent’s estimated US$1.5 trillion in annual trade took place between African countries.

“Right now, the added value in manufacturing of Africa stands at less than 2 per cent, whereas the overall trade of African countries amounts to $1.5 trillion U.S. dollars. And just 15 per cent is accounted for by the transactions within the African continent.

“And yet the situation is shifting thanks to the success of the AfCFTA. A contribution is made to production and cooperation in industry to gain economic independence,” he stated.

He pointed to the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) as an important mechanism for expanding regional commerce, strengthening industrial cooperation and reducing Africa’s dependence on external markets.

The summit also provides a platform for Russia to deepen its economic and political engagement with African countries, as Moscow seeks to expand cooperation in trade, technology, energy and security.

Russia offers to expand agricultural and technology cooperation

Mr Putin said Russia was prepared to share technological expertise with African countries, support infrastructure development and expand cooperation in agriculture.

He disclosed that Russia had supplied approximately 13 million tonnes of agricultural products to Africa during the first nine months of 2026, adding that more than 40 African countries had received Russian grain and fertilisers.

He also said Russia was supporting efforts to improve Africa’s debt situation through joint programmes designed to provide financing for economic growth.

“Russia is helping improve the debt situation in Africa. We have a number of joint programmes with a number of African countries. And these programmes are meant to lend money to finance growth,” he said.

The Russian president further called for African countries to have a stronger voice in international financial institutions, including the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and the World Bank.

He argued that the institutions’ decision-making structures should better reflect the interests and priorities of developing economies.

The summit forms part of broader efforts by Russia and African countries to expand diplomatic and economic cooperation. Its discussions are expected to address ways to strengthen trade and investment ties, support industrial development and increase collaboration in technology and other strategic sectors.

Ghana News.title: Supreme Court won’t settle a debate through constitutional interpretation – Kwaku Azar on NPP presidential term limit suit
Ghana News.content:
Legal scholar Kwaku Azar Asare has questioned whether the New Patriotic Party’s (NPP) suit at the Supreme Court seeking an interpretation of the presidential term limit presents a justiciable constitutional dispute or amounts to a request for an advisory opinion.

The NPP has filed a suit at the Supreme Court seeking an interpretation of Article 66(2) of the 1992 Constitution, which provides for a presidential term of four years and limits a person to two terms in office.

The party is seeking a declaration that the two-term limit applies whether the terms are consecutive or non-consecutive.

The action has drawn attention to the constitutional implications of presidential term limits ahead of the 2028 general election. However, the filing of the suit does not, in itself, establish that President John Dramani Mahama intends to seek another term.

In a Facebook post, Mr Asare argued that the party’s action appeared to differ from previous constitutional cases it pursued, including the 31st December Case and a challenge to police permit requirements for public demonstrations.

He said those cases involved identifiable government actions or existing laws alleged to be inconsistent with the Constitution, rather than disagreements over constitutional interpretation in the abstract.

“Notice something important about these cases. The NPP of yore challenged identifiable governmental actions and existing laws that allegedly violated the Constitution. The Court was not being invited merely to settle an interesting public debate,” he wrote.

Mr Asare argued that the current writ had not identified an allegedly unconstitutional enactment, act or omission requiring judicial intervention.

“What enactment is being challenged? What unconstitutional act or omission is alleged? Nobody has filed to contest a third presidential election. No electoral authority has determined that a person who has already been elected President twice is eligible for a third election,” he stated.

“At best, on the facts reported, there is a public debate over what the Constitution permits.”

He maintained that disagreement over the meaning of a constitutional provision does not, by itself, establish a justiciable controversy.

To support his argument, Mr Asare cited Bilson v Attorney-General [1993-94] 1 GLR 104, a Supreme Court decision concerning the limits of its jurisdiction to interpret constitutional provisions in the absence of an actual dispute.

“The Court held that it had jurisdiction to interpret constitutional provisions in the context of disputes, but no jurisdiction to tender advice to prospective litigants,” he wrote.

Mr Asare said the case illustrated the distinction between resolving a genuine constitutional dispute and providing judicial guidance on a hypothetical question.

He argued that the distinction was important in determining whether the NPP’s action met the threshold for judicial consideration.

Mr Asare also referred to Ex parte Akosah, a case associated with the principles governing when questions of constitutional interpretation arise and should be referred to the Supreme Court.

He cautioned against relying on the decision to suggest that every disagreement over constitutional meaning automatically warrants the Court’s intervention.

“But an important qualification is often overlooked. Ex parte Akosah arose in the context of determining when a lower court should refer a constitutional interpretation question to the Supreme Court. It was not an invitation to citizens to manufacture competing interpretations and demand that the Supreme Court resolve them,” he argued.

He added that competing views expressed by lawyers, academics and political commentators did not automatically create a justiciable constitutional controversy.

“Citizens, lawyers, academics, and political parties are free to express different views about the meaning of constitutional provisions. That is healthy constitutional discourse. But merely because someone advances a different interpretation does not mean the Supreme Court must be invited to settle the disagreement,” he wrote.

Mr Asare urged the Supreme Court to exercise restraint in determining which constitutional questions require judicial intervention.

“The Supreme Court is a court of law, not a constitutional advice centre. And the Court itself must remain disciplined, resisting the temptation to wade into every constitutional controversy merely because the question is politically important, intellectually interesting, or generating considerable public attention,” he stated.

He argued that scarce judicial resources should be directed towards resolving genuine disputes rather than providing what he described as constitutional consultations.

Mr Asare suggested that if the writ failed to disclose a justiciable cause of action, the Court should dismiss it at the earliest procedurally appropriate stage.

He proposed a brief ruling dismissing the action for want of jurisdiction, without prejudice to a properly constituted case arising from a justiciable controversy.

Ghana News.title: President Ruto confirms Bayern Munich vs Ajax clash to open Kenya’s new stadium
Ghana News.content:
Kenya President William Ruto has confirmed that Bayern Munich and Ajax will play the opening match at the country’s new national stadium on January 5, 2027, as Nairobi prepares to welcome two of European football’s most decorated clubs.

Announcing the fixture in a national address on Wednesday, Ruto said the match would mark the official opening of the 60,000-capacity Raila Odinga International Stadium, formerly known as Talanta Stadium, in Nairobi.

“Come January 5, 2027, we will open this stadium with a historic match between two giants of European football, FC Bayern Munich of Germany and FC Ajax of Amsterdam. Between them, they have been crowned champions of Europe ten times,” Ruto said.

The German champions and Dutch giants will meet at the new venue, which is expected to host matches during the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations, co-hosted by Kenya, Uganda and Tanzania.

Ruto also highlighted the symbolism behind the fixture, linking Bayern’s German roots to the late former Kenyan Prime Minister Raila Amolo Odinga, after whom the stadium has been named, and Ajax’s reputation for developing young talent.

“On January 5, 2027, talent and the future will meet in Nairobi,” he added.

The President said the event would be delivered through corporate partnerships and a commercial model designed to attract private investment and create opportunities for Kenyans.

Both clubs have confirmed the fixture. Ajax described the invitation as an honour, while Bayern said the event would strengthen its connection with supporters across Africa. The match will also serve as a major football occasion ahead of Kenya’s preparations for AFCON 2027.

Ghana News.title: Underage girl, two others arrested over death of mobile money vendor at Kasoa guest house
Ghana News.content:
Police have arrested three suspects in connection with the murder of 34-year-old mobile money vendor Christian Amponsah, whose body was discovered at a guest house around Kasoa Second in the Central Region.

The Central East Regional Police Command said the suspects, identified as 59-year-old Felicia Osei Appiah, 24-year-old Clement Opoku Yeboah and a female juvenile, were arrested on Tuesday, October 27, 2026.

According to the police, the arrests followed investigations into the death of Amponsah after the manager of the guest house reported discovering the victim lying motionless in a room.

The manager told police that the deceased and the juvenile had checked into the guest house and booked a room for two hours. When the booking period elapsed and neither occupant emerged, he went to check on them.

He reportedly discovered Amponsah lying motionless in a pool of blood, prompting a report to the police.

Officers who visited the scene found the deceased lying face down, with bedsheets, curtains and pillows covering his body.

The body was subsequently conveyed to the Police Hospital Mortuary in Accra for preservation, identification and autopsy.

The three suspects are currently in police custody and assisting with investigations as authorities work to establish the circumstances surrounding the killing and the respective roles, if any, of those arrested.

The Command said investigations were ongoing and that steps were being taken to put the suspects before court.

Ghana News.title: Ghana signs deal with Russia’s Tatarstan for jobs, business, academic research and cultural exchanges
Ghana News.content:
Ghana has signed a Memorandum of Understanding with Russia’s Republic of Tatarstan to facilitate employment opportunities for Ghanaian citizens under the Alabuga Start programme.

The agreement was signed between the Ministry of Labour, Jobs and Employment and the Alabuga Special Economic Zone, with the aim of strengthening cooperation in the employment of Ghanaian citizens.

Among the officials present at the signing were E.R. Safiullin, Acting Director of Alabuga; Senator Muhametshin; Gatin, an adviser to the Rais of Tatarstan; and Ahmetshin, Permanent Representative of Tatarstan to Moscow.

Speaking after the signing in Russia, Minister for Labour, Jobs and Employment, Emmanuel Kwadwo Agyekum, said the agreement would open up opportunities for Ghana’s youthful population to access jobs with competitive salaries, accommodation and residence permits.

He said the government was committed to ensuring that Ghanaians recruited under the arrangement received appropriate employment opportunities and adequate protection.

“We’re going to make sure that they get the right jobs to do, they are protected, they are being given the right conditions of service,” he said.

Kwadwo Agyekum explained that the agreement extends beyond labour migration, with both parties exploring opportunities for business collaboration, academic research, and cultural and religious exchanges.

He said Ghanaian businesses were expected to participate in upcoming business forums, while universities and academic institutions would be encouraged to collaborate on research initiatives.

The Minister added that the government would continue pursuing international partnerships aimed at expanding employment opportunities for young people.

Ghana News.title: UG asks students to suspend planned demonstration after talks
Ghana News.content:
The University of Ghana has asked a group of students to suspend a planned demonstration following engagements with the university’s management over their concerns, including accommodation.

In a notice dated Wednesday, October 28, the Office of the Dean of Student Affairs said the Dean, Professor Rosina Kyerematen, had engaged the organisers and assured them of management’s commitment to addressing students’ immediate, medium-term and long-term needs.

The notice said the organisers had consequently been advised to suspend the planned demonstration while further engagements with management and other stakeholders continue.

“The Dean of Student Affairs has subsequently engaged the group on their concerns and assured them of Management's commitment to addressing the immediate, middle-term, and long-term needs of students; including accommodation,” the notice stated.

The university also reminded students and student groups to follow established procedures when addressing grievances, in accordance with the regulations governing junior members of the university.

It said the Office of Student Affairs was working with various university units, including the Student Financial Aid Office and the Careers and Counselling Directorate, to provide welfare support and promote a peaceful learning environment.

Ghana News.title: Kufuor condemns vote buying, says it undermines voters’ dignity
Ghana News.content:
Former President John Agyekum Kufuor has condemned vote buying, warning that politicians who pay for votes undermine the dignity of citizens and risk treating the electorate as people they have purchased.

He has urged political leaders to respect voters’ rights and recognise that electoral victory comes with a responsibility to serve and remain accountable to the people.

Speaking in an interview with Evans Mensah on JoyNews’ PM Express, Mr Kufuor said any government that disregards the rights and dignity of citizens betrays the trust placed in it.

“The humanity of each and every one of us is captured in this land. Any government that would come and look down upon any of us like people that should not be accorded the rights and entitlements as owners of this land, that government is a traitor. It has betrayed us,” he said.

Mr Kufuor said his commitment to democracy was rooted in his belief that every citizen was entitled to equal dignity and political rights.

“I'm a democrat, and it's all because I acknowledge every individual within this land we call our nation. I acknowledge you as entitled as me; you are sovereign. And this is why I respect the vote,” he said.

He described voting as the means through which citizens delegate political authority to elected leaders, stressing that those entrusted with power must remain accountable to the electorate.

“Not all of us could go and sit in Jubilee House as government. We have to use the vote to give my power to the person I'm voting for to go. And if I give my power to you to go and govern the land through a government, then this government should be accountable to me. That's where accountability comes from,” he said.

The former President described the buying and selling of votes as an aberration and a form of corruption that should not be tolerated.

He argued that candidates who offer money or other inducements in exchange for votes show disrespect for voters and undermine the principle of freely choosing political representatives.

“You come in, and you want to come and bribe me or buy me, then you don't respect me at all. You're coming to take my birthright from me, and then you get there because you paid me. If you bought me, then you do with me as you want. And that's the utter corruption that shouldn't be tolerated at all. It's wrong,” he said.

Mr Kufuor added that anyone seeking political office should approach the responsibility with deep respect for the citizens whose mandate they seek.

He criticised the practice of offering voters money in exchange for electoral support, arguing that such transactions could weaken citizens’ ability to demand accountability from elected officials.

“That's all because we've been enslaved and abused and treated like subhumans for far too long. So somebody comes and gives you in the village a hundred cedis, a thousand cedis, so you go and vote for that person. And he comes in here to govern you. He's paid for you. He's bought you. And then he mistreats you,” he said.

Asked whether efforts to address vote buying should begin within political parties, Mr Kufuor said the responsibility extended across society.

He urged citizens to recognise the value of their votes and resist attempts to influence their choices through gifts or other material inducements.

“Everybody should take responsibility. Look at your wife. If you didn't have a piece of the power of the land, would you have the right to vote as the Constitution provides? So that vote that's given you as an individual, if you really respect yourself and you understand what the whole thing is about, you won't go and sell it off,” he said.

He cautioned voters against accepting material items in exchange for their electoral choices.

“You won't allow anybody to come and give you whatever it is, television or these days the way the report comes,” he added.

Ghana News.title: Kufuor blames vanity and vindictiveness for Ghana’s poor policy continuity
Ghana News.content:
Former President John Agyekum Kufuor has blamed vanity, vindictiveness and a lack of vision among successive governments for Ghana’s failure to sustain some of the socio-economic initiatives introduced by previous administrations.

He said the tendency of incoming governments to abandon policies and agreements initiated by their predecessors had undermined opportunities for investment, institutional development and long-term national progress.

Speaking in an interview with Evans Mensah on JoyNews’ PM Express, Mr Kufuor cited the cancellation of an agreement his administration negotiated with Barclays International as an example of what he described as a failure to appreciate the long-term benefits of policy continuity.

“We got that agreement with Barclays International after three years of hard work. We opened offices at Airport City. We left office in 2008,” he recalled.

He said the government that succeeded his administration moved to cancel the agreement around 2009, reportedly citing concerns that it could facilitate money laundering.

“By 2009 or so, the government that succeeded mine came out to cancel the agreement. Perhaps they didn't see how we saw it and the disciplines that we had put in it. The excuse they gave was that they suspected that our agreement might lead to money laundering,” he said.

The former President argued that the decision to cancel the agreement may have been taken without sufficient consideration of the reasons behind his administration’s partnership with the international financial institution.

“I would only say perhaps they just didn't do their homework to understand why we went into that,” he said.

Mr Kufuor maintained that the arrangement could have helped Ghana attract foreign capital and encouraged greater financial discipline within government.

“I'm sure a lot of people even from Europe and so-called advanced parts of the world would have brought their capital here,” he said.

He added that the presence of such an institution would have required the government to maintain standards capable of sustaining investor confidence.

Asked why successive governments often reverse decisions made by their predecessors, Mr Kufuor pointed to personal and political considerations.

“The other too is some vanity. We want to show we perhaps are better than the people we are succeeding,” he said.

He also cited vindictiveness and the pursuit of political power as factors that could undermine the continuity of public policies.

Mr Kufuor argued that political office should not be treated as a means of personal advancement but as a responsibility entrusted to leaders by the electorate.

The former President said elected leaders must recognise that their authority derives from the people and should be exercised in the public interest.

“When they trust, they give it to you. They give it to you as a trustee to use it to manage to the betterment of all, inclusively,” he said.

He warned that leaders who failed to appreciate this responsibility risked becoming preoccupied with personal aggrandisement and political rivalries at the expense of national development.

“If you do not understand this as the cornerstone and you take the power, then you begin to get aggrandizement. You become like a lord. You may use lies, vindictiveness, petty jealousies and all. So keep on wallowing. You don't have vision. It's a huge problem,” he said.

He cited the success of the Kufuor Foundation's scholarship programme, which selects students online and mentors them through their university education.

"Since we launched this foundation, you'd be surprised. The panel of selectors, they've been good. They go in. I believe the applicants apply online. So it's not who you know. It's not Kufuor sons and daughters," he stated.

He noted that one of the scholars is now the President of the Comoros Youth Council in Britain, while another is pursuing a PhD at Oxford University and has been elected President of Christ Church students.

"It shows that one of these days these people are going to come back," he said.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.title: Russian authorities detain suspect over St. Petersburg cafe blast
World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”
