World.title: Fidelity Bank Plc redeems $400m eurobond at maturity
World.content:
Fidelity Bank Plc has redeemed its 5-year $400 million Senior Unsecured Notes at maturity, reaffirming its commitment to meeting investor obligations and reinforcing its track record in the international debt capital markets.

Issued on 28 October 2021, the 5-year Eurobond matured on 28 October 2026 and carried an annual coupon of 7.625 per cent, payable semi-annually. Fidelity Bank met all scheduled coupon payments throughout the life of the instrument and has now fulfilled its final repayment obligation in full, covering both principal and accrued interest.

The redemption was funded from internally generated liquidity as part of the bank’s forward-looking liquidity management strategy. Through a dedicated sinking fund, Fidelity Bank progressively provided for the maturing obligation, enabling the bank to meet its commitment while maintaining business-as-usual operations and compliance with applicable regulatory liquidity requirements.

Commenting on the development, Fidelity Bank Plc’s Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer, Nneka Onyeali-Ikpe, said the successful redemption reflected the bank’s disciplined approach to financial management and its commitment to delivering on its obligations.

“This successful redemption demonstrates the strength of our franchise, the discipline of our balance sheet management and our commitment to honouring our obligations to investors and other stakeholders. We anticipated this maturity from the outset and planned accordingly, which reflects our commitment to responsible financial management,” Mrs Onyeali-Ikpe said.

The redemption further strengthens Fidelity Bank’s record in the international debt capital markets. The 2021 issuance marked the bank’s third Eurobond transaction, following earlier issuances in 2013 and 2017, in which the bank raised $300 million and $400 million, respectively. The 2021 offer attracted investor orders exceeding US$700 million, reflecting strong demand for the bank’s international debt offering.

The successful Eurobond redemption follows the completion of Fidelity Bank’s recapitalisation programme ahead of the regulatory deadline. The bank’s capital-raising efforts increased its eligible regulatory capital to approximately N533 billion, exceeding the N500 billion minimum capital requirement for banks with international authorisation.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The completion of these milestones underscores Fidelity Bank’s strong capital position, prudent liquidity management and disciplined approach to financial execution. It also reinforces the Bank’s capacity to meet its financial obligations while pursuing its strategic growth objectives across domestic and international markets.

World.title: FG disburses N249.6bn health fund in three years, targets 17,600 facilities
World.content:
The federal government says it has disbursed N249.6 billion to the Basic Health Care Provision Fund (BHCPF) in the past three years, representing 77.1 per cent of the N323.6 billion disbursed since the fund was established in 2019.

The government also plans to expand direct financing to at least 17,600 primary healthcare facilities and provide health insurance coverage for about 90,000 Nigerians in correctional facilities.

The Minister of State for Health and Social Welfare, Iziaq Salako, disclosed this on Wednesday in Abuja during a ministerial briefing on three years of implementation of the fund under President Bola Tinubu’s administration.

Established under the National Health Act 2014, the BHCPF is designed to improve access to essential healthcare, particularly for poor and vulnerable Nigerians.

Mr Salako said the fund had become a key instrument for implementing the Nigeria Health Sector Renewal Investment Initiative, launched in December 2023 to strengthen healthcare delivery and financing.

Disbursements and allocations

According to Mr Salako, total releases to the fund stood at N422.3 billion as of September 2026, with N323.6 billion disbursed.

He said the Ministerial Oversight Committee approved an additional N40.76 billion at its meeting on 14 October. The approval is expected to raise cumulative disbursements to N364.3 billion, including N290.2 billion under the Tinubu administration, according to the statement.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Speaking on the latest allocation, Mr Salako said N19.87 billion would go to the National Health Insurance Authority, N18.34 billion to the National Primary Health Care Development Agency, N2.04 billion to emergency medical treatment and N509.48 million to the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention.

He said the allocations would support health insurance, primary healthcare services, emergency medical response and disease surveillance.

Mr Salako added that the government was working with the National Assembly to increase the fund’s statutory allocation from one per cent to two per cent of the Consolidated Revenue Fund.

Health insurance and primary healthcare

On financial protection, Mr Salako said national health insurance enrolment increased from about 16.2 million people in 2023 to 23.06 million by the third quarter of 2026.

He said the BHCPF had supported insurance coverage for 3,182,943 vulnerable Nigerians with National Identification Numbers.

The fund, he added, had also supported free surgeries and rehabilitation for women with vesicovaginal fistula, emergency caesarean sections and other emergency obstetric and newborn care interventions for 96,068 women and babies.

Mr Salako said the oversight committee had also approved health insurance coverage for approximately 90,000 Nigerians in correctional facilities, with implementation expected to expand access to essential healthcare for inmates.

On primary healthcare delivery, he said direct facility financing currently supports 8,309 PHCs across the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory.

He said the government planned to include a further 5,212 facilities, bringing the projected total to 13,521. However, the government’s broader target is to expand direct financing to at least 17,600 facilities.

Mr Salako added that the number of facilities attaining Level 2 readiness increased from 1,748 in 2024 to 3,202 in the third quarter of 2026.

He also said PHC attendance rose from 34.55 million in 2023 to 43.06 million by the second quarter of 2026.

Emergency services and health workers

On emergency medical services, Mr Salako said operational structures had been established in all 36 states and the FCT.

Through the Rural Emergency Service and Maternal Transport arrangements, emergency transport services had been established in 171 of the 172 local government areas covered by the Maternal and Newborn Mortality Reduction Innovation Initiative. The government plans to extend the initiative to 200 local government areas by December 2026.

He said the emergency response system had recorded 168,571 ambulance service episodes since 2023, covering obstetric emergencies, neonatal and under-five emergencies, road traffic injuries, snakebites, burns and other urgent medical conditions.

Mr Salako said 78,054 frontline health workers had been trained towards a national target of 120,000.

He also said the oversight committee approved phased salary support for 13,800 community-based health workers and skilled birth attendants. Under the arrangement, the federal government would cover eligible salary costs in full in the first year, 67 per cent in the second year and 33 per cent in the third year, before state governments assume full responsibility.

He said the committee had also approved the operationalisation of MEDIPOOL, a pooled procurement mechanism intended to improve access to essential medicines and health commodities, subject to quality assurance and accountability safeguards.

Accountability and next steps

Mr Salako urged state governments to fulfil their counterpart financing obligations and ensure sustainable funding for primary healthcare services. He commended Katsina State for releasing N240.79 million to its State Health Insurance Agency to support expanded coverage.

He said the Ministry of Health and Social Welfare was strengthening financial accountability through the implementation of the updated BHCPF Guidelines 2.0 and collaboration with the Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission to track the use of public funds.

He emphasised that timely reporting, transparent payments, and expenditure verification were necessary to ensure funds reached healthcare facilities and translated into services for patients.

Mr Salako said the government remained committed to increasing domestic health financing and improving access to essential healthcare, particularly for vulnerable Nigerians.

World.title: Senate asks Tinubu to rename education institution after late Afenifere leader, Reuben Fasoranti
World.content:
The Senate on Wednesday called on the federal government to immortalise the late National Leader of Afenifere, the pan-Yoruba socio-political organisation, Reuben Fasoranti, who died last week at the age of 100.

The upper chamber recommended that an educational institution be renamed after the late elder statesman in recognition of his contributions to the advancement of education in South-west Nigeria.

The lawmakers adopted the resolution following a motion sponsored by Adeniyi Adegbonmire (APC, Ondo Central) during plenary.

Mr Fasoranti died last Tuesday. President Bola Tinubu, Ondo State Governor Lucky Aiyedatiwa and other governors in the South-west have mourned his death.

Moving the motion, Mr Adegbonmire, who chairs the Senate Committee on Judiciary, Human Rights and Legal Matters, said the late elder statesman’s contributions to education profoundly influenced his approach to governance, particularly his emphasis on human welfare and humanitarian service.

The senator described the late Fasoranti as a committed follower of the late nationalist and politician, Obafemi Awolowo, who led the Action Group during the First Republic and later became associated with the Unity Party of Nigeria (UPN) during the Second Republic.

He also noted that Mr Fasoranti was among prominent Nigerians who opposed military rule and advocated the restoration of democratic governance.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“Pa Fasoranti remained steadfast in the struggle for democracy. He was a man who spoke truth to power, honest and upright. He saw and promoted the need to collaborate with other socio-political organisations, such as Arewa and Ohanaeze Ndigbo, towards having a better Nigeria. He believed in one united and prosperous Nigeria and promoted this all through his life,” Mr Adegbonmire said.

The senator also urged his colleagues to constitute a delegation to convey the Senate’s condolences to the people of Ondo State and the deceased’s family.

Jide Ipinsagba, the senator representing Ondo North, supported the motion, describing the late Fasoranti as an advocate who contributed immensely to Nigeria’s educational development and promoted peace in Yorubaland and across the country.

The Deputy Senate President, Barau Jibrin, who presided over the session, approved the prayers of the motion and directed senators to observe a minute’s silence in honour of the late elder statesman.

World.title: Police, youth clash in Ondo community over farmer’s murder
World.content:
The gruesome murder of a farmer in Ala community, in Akure North Local Government Area, Ondo State has degenerated into a violent clash between a group of youth in the area and police operatives who attempted to prevent them from taking the law into their own hands.

It was gathered that the youth attempted to lynch the murder suspects, but were prevented by the police, resulting in a mob reaction from the youth.

A farmer, Rasheed Hassan, was killed on his farm last week by the suspects, who also robbed him of his belongings.

Trouble, however, broke out when some youth leaders arrested suspected culprits and handed them over to the police.

Reports say the angry youth of the town attacked the police station where the suspects were held in custody in an attempt to get them executed extrajudicially. The result was a clash with police operatives who resisted their efforts.

Residents say the situation created tensions in the community since Monday, with police reinforcement pouring into the area and effecting several arrests.

The Ondo State Police Command, which confirmed the development, condemned the mob attack.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Police spokesperson, Jimoh Abayomi, said the ensuing melee followed an attempt by an angry crowd to take the law into its own hands over the suspected murder of a farmer.

“The incident followed the killing of one Rasheed Hassan, a farmer, whose death was reported to the police on October 24, 2026, from General Camp in the Government Reserve area. Upon receiving the report, police operatives visited the scene and recovered the victim’s body,” Mr Abayomi said in a statement on Wednesday.

“Preliminary observations revealed deep cuts to the victim’s head and other parts of his body, while his belongings were reportedly missing.

“Investigations immediately commenced to identify and apprehend those responsible for the killing.”

He, however, said the chaos occurred when the Ala Youth President, popularly called Olori Odo, reportedly arrested two suspects on 26 October.

“While conveying the suspects to the police station for necessary action, he was confronted by an angry mob demanding that the suspects be handed over for extrajudicial killing,” Mr Abayomi said.

“He subsequently sought refuge at the Ala Divisional Police Headquarters with the suspects. However, the mob pursued them and launched an attack on the police facility.”

He said the mob reportedly became increasingly violent, throwing stones and other dangerous objects at the station while resisting efforts by police rescue teams to gain access to the area.

“In response to the escalating violence, tactical and other rescue teams were deployed to restore order and protect lives. At about 0145 hours on October 27, 2026, police operatives successfully rescued the two suspects from the mob,” he said.

“However, the patrol team conveying the suspects back to Akure came under attack. During the incident, two police officers sustained gunshot injuries from pellets allegedly fired from a youth pump-action firearm. The injured officers were immediately rushed to a nearby hospital for urgent medical attention.

“Following the attack, operatives of the Command arrested fourteen (14) suspects in connection with the assault on police officers and the attack on the police facility and rescue team. Investigations are ongoing to establish the individual roles of those arrested and ensure that anyone found culpable faces the full weight of the law.

“The Command has maintained tactical deployment in the area to prevent any further breakdown of law and order. Normalcy has since returned to the community, while security monitoring continues.”

Meanwhile, the Commissioner of Police, Felix Ohagwu, has condemned the attack on police officers and the police facility, describing mob action and attempts to obstruct lawful police operations as unacceptable.

He said no individual or group has the right to take the law into their own hands, regardless of the gravity of any alleged crime. He warned that the Command would not tolerate attacks on police facilities, assaults on officers or any attempt to undermine lawful police operations.

The Commissioner of Police further assured residents that the circumstances surrounding the farmer’s death and the violence that followed were being thoroughly investigated. He emphasised that all those found culpable would be dealt with in accordance with the law.

He urged members of the public to remain calm, cooperate with security agencies and provide credible information that could assist the ongoing investigations.

He also appealed to community leaders and youth groups to discourage mob action and encourage residents to allow the criminal justice system to take its course.

World.title: Zenith Bank expands digital payment options with Google Pay launch
World.content:
Zenith Bank Plc has announced today that its customers can now pay with Google Pay, bringing greater convenience and security to everyday transactions. By adding an eligible Zenith Bank card to Google Wallet, customers can tap to pay at participating contactless payment terminals and check out online or in apps without repeatedly entering their card details.

As Nigerians increasingly rely on their phones to shop, pay bills and manage their finances, Zenith Bank continues to advance banking experiences that combine convenience with robust security.

A simpler, more secure way to pay

Google Pay uses payment tokenization, a technology that replaces a customer’s actual card number with a digital token. This helps protect sensitive payment information by reducing the need to share actual card details during transactions.

For Zenith Bank customers, this means:

• Enhanced security: Tokenization helps protect actual card details, reducing their exposure during payments.

• Faster checkout: Customers can tap their compatible phones at participating contactless terminals or pay online without repeatedly entering their card information.

• Convenience across channels: Eligible cards can be used through supported digital payment experiences, subject to device, merchant and service compatibility.

• Greater peace of mind: Built-in security features help customers make digital payments with greater confidence.

A legacy of innovation, a future of possibilities

Zenith Bank’s latest digital payment development builds on a history of using technology to improve customer experience.

In 2007, the Bank opened what it describes as Nigeria’s first ATM gallery, a full-fledged branch without human tellers that offered customers access to cash, including on weekends and public holidays. At a time when conventional banking often meant lengthy queues, the initiative provided an alternative built around convenience and accessibility.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Today, the same commitment to innovation continues to shape the Bank’s digital ambitions.

The Group Managing Director/CEO of Zenith Bank Plc, Dr Adaora Umeoji, underscored the importance of the technology, describing it as “digitally forward.” She added that the upcoming Zenith Bank Tech Fair 2026, themed Future Forward 6.0 and scheduled for November 5, would take the conversation further.

How to get started

Eligible Zenith Bank cardholders can add their supported cards to Google Wallet on compatible devices by opening the app, selecting the option to add a payment card and completing the required verification process.

Once set up, customers can use Google Pay at participating contactless terminals and supported online or in-app checkout points. Availability is subject to card eligibility, device compatibility and merchant acceptance.

About Zenith Bank Plc

Zenith Bank Plc is a leading financial services institution committed to delivering innovative banking solutions, superior customer service and sustainable value to its stakeholders. Through continuous investment in technology, operational excellence and customer-centric innovation, the Bank continues to advance digital banking and support the evolving financial needs of individuals, businesses and communities.

World.title: Environmental group opposes proposed naval base in Akwa Ibom forest reserve
World.content:
An environmental organisation, Peer Foundation, has opposed plans to establish a naval base in the disputed Stubbs Creek Forest Reserve in Akwa Ibom State, warning that the project could deepen environmental degradation and heighten tensions with host communities.

The organisation, in a statement signed by its Executive Director, Mfon Gabriel, on Monday, demanded that Akwa Ibom and federal governments reverse the decision and halt industrial activities within the reserve.

The proposed naval base was announced by the state government as part of efforts to strengthen security along the coastline and protect critical oil and gas infrastructure.

The state Commissioner for Internal Security and Waterways, Koko Essien, disclosed the plan during a ministerial briefing in Uyo, according to media reports.

Peer Foundation argued that establishing a military facility in the reserve without adequate consultation with affected communities could undermine their livelihoods, access to ancestral lands and environmental rights.

The organisation alleged that the proposal was part of a pattern of using security infrastructure to facilitate commercial activities in the forest, including petroleum-related projects.

It also called for the withdrawal of what it described as “destructive” refinery plans and the commencement of a community-led forest restoration programme.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Forest under pressure

The dispute over the proposed naval base occurs amid longstanding concerns about the destruction of Stubbs Creek Forest Reserve, which spans parts of Eket, Esit Eket, Ibeno and Mbo local government areas.

In a November 2025 report, PREMIUM TIMES documented how road construction and the BUA refinery project contributed to the loss of forest cover and raised concerns about the future of the reserve.

The report, titled “How refinery and highway project wiped out Akwa Ibom’s Stubbs Creek Forest,” also examined questions surrounding compliance with the legal procedures for removing protected forest land from reserve status.

Another PREMIUM TIMES report, published in 2026, examined the environmental risks associated with the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway’s proposed route through the reserve.

The report cited a study that estimated the climate damage associated with emissions from the proposed highway route at about N785 billion, highlighting the potential cost of further disturbance to the forest.

The reserve is an important ecological habitat, supporting wildlife and providing resources for communities that depend on the forest for their livelihoods. Most importantly, the Stubbs Creek Forest Reserve serves as a buffer between Akwa Ibom land and the Atlantic Ocean.

‘Community engagement should precede announcement’

Peer Foundation said the government failed to obtain the free, prior and informed consent of indigenous communities before announcing the proposed naval base.

It argued that decisions affecting the forest should not be made without involving residents whose livelihoods, cultural heritage and access to natural resources could be affected.

The organisation also warned that introducing a military installation without adequate community engagement could generate mistrust and tensions between residents and security personnel.

It said the presence of a naval base near petroleum infrastructure could also raise concerns about whether security operations would prioritise the protection of corporate assets over the rights and welfare of host communities.

“National security cannot exist at the expense of ecological survival,” the organisation said.

It described Stubbs Creek as a vital carbon sink and natural barrier against coastal erosion, warning that clearing more forest for infrastructure could worsen environmental damage.

The group also said the forest provides medicinal resources and supports local livelihoods, including activities tied to the area’s natural resources.

Dispute over the reserve

The proposed naval base adds another dimension to the longstanding dispute over the management, ownership and development of Stubbs Creek Forest Reserve.

The Akwa Ibom State Government has previously rejected claims that the forest belongs exclusively to the Ekid people, arguing that the reserve is administered by the state under applicable laws.

In a report published in January 2026, PREMIUM TIMES examined leaked government memoranda that appeared to support the Ekid people’s claims to parts of the reserve.

The dispute has also centred on whether the relevant legal procedures for changing the status of protected portions of the forest were followed before development projects were undertaken.

Peer Foundation called on the state and federal governments to prioritise ecological restoration, environmental accountability and community participation over further industrial development in the reserve.

The organisation said it would pursue its opposition through legal and peaceful means.

The Akwa Ibom State Government said it wants the naval base to improve security along the coastline and protect strategic infrastructure. However, further details on the proposed facility’s implementation, its precise location, and the environmental safeguards to be applied were not provided in the available announcement.

World.title: 68 killed as two Spanish high-speed trains collide
World.content:
At least 68 people have been killed after a high-speed train collided with another train in Spain’s Toledo province. The transport minister blamed an “inexplicable” decision by the rail control centre following a computer malfunction.

The Castilla-La Mancha regional government confirmed the death toll on Wednesday and said 58 other people required hospital treatment. Rescue workers continued searching the wreckage for survivors and victims of the crash, which involved two trains carrying more than 500 passengers.

The collision occurred in the morning between the towns of Urda and Los Yébenes, south of Madrid, according to Spain’s rail infrastructure operator, ADIF.

A train operated by state-owned Renfe struck the rear of a stationary train operated by private company Iryo. The impact knocked two carriages of the Iryo train off the tracks and left several carriages severely damaged.

The Associated Press (AP) reported that the collision occurred on a stretch of track surrounded by olive fields. Debris from the wreckage was scattered down a gravel slope.

Minister blames control centre

Spain’s Transport Minister, Óscar Puente, quoted by AP, said the crash followed a computer malfunction that disrupted a section of the railway before the control centre instructed the Renfe train to resume its journey without speed restrictions.

According to Mr Puente, the railway’s security system stopped working at about 8:30 a.m. because of a computer malfunction, forcing trains operating along a 63-kilometre stretch to stop.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

He said the control centre subsequently instructed the Renfe train to resume movement, although a stop signal remained active on the line.

The train collided with the stationary Iryo train at about 8:53 a.m.

Mr Puente said the Renfe train should not have been allowed to move while the stop signal remained active. He added that, if it had been permitted to proceed, it should have been instructed to travel at a reduced speed.

The minister said investigators were still examining the available information to establish the train’s speed at the time of the collision. He said it could have been travelling at 200 kilometres per hour on that section of track.

“I am not attributing responsibility to anyone, I am just stating the facts,” he said.

Mr Puente said the train engineers were not to blame for the crash.

Survivors recount chaotic scenes

Passengers described a violent impact that sent luggage and mobile phones flying through the train carriages.

Ignacio Relaño, who was travelling on the Renfe train, told Spanish public broadcaster TVE that the train briefly stopped before moving again and colliding with the Iryo train.

“We all felt the train abruptly slowing down and then the impact,” he said.

“The car leaned to one side like it was about to tip over. I hit my nose, everything went flying, luggage, cell phones. Everything shook.”

AP reported another passenger saying that she was thrown forward when the train braked suddenly, breaking the small table in front of her. She said she saw injured passengers and people trapped in the wreckage.

Spain’s Health Minister, Mónica García, said emergency workers were concentrating on recovering survivors and bodies from the two most severely damaged carriages. The injured were being taken to hospitals in the surrounding area.

“It was a high-speed impact, so we are expecting this to be a tragedy,” she said.

The two trains were carrying 544 passengers, according to figures provided by the regional authorities. The Renfe train had 397 passengers, while the Iryo train carried 147.

Iryo, an Italian-owned railway company, said it had activated its security protocols and was working closely with the authorities.

Emergency response, rail disruption

The crash prompted the suspension of rail services between Madrid, Ciudad Real and Andalusia, according to the BBC.

Emergency services, including firefighters and police, were deployed to the scene, while a military emergency brigade was mobilised to support rescue operations. Ambulances and medical helicopters transported injured passengers, while survivors who escaped without serious injuries were moved away from the site by bus.

Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez cancelled his scheduled engagements to focus on the disaster.

In a post on X, Mr Sánchez said he was “dismayed by the serious train accident in Toledo” and expressed sympathy for the victims and their families.

Spain’s King Felipe VI and Queen Letizia also expressed condolences to the families of those killed and support for the injured.

European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said Europe shared in the grief of the victims’ families.

Spain’s football federation postponed all 24 Copa del Rey matches scheduled for Wednesday following the crash.

Second deadly train collision this year

AP reported that the disaster has renewed concerns about Spain’s high-speed rail network, which had been a source of national pride since its introduction in 1992.

Before this year, the country had not recorded a fatal crash on its dedicated high-speed rail lines since the network opened.

In January, 46 people were killed in another collision involving trains operated by Iryo and Renfe in southern Spain. An Iryo train derailed and struck an oncoming Renfe train, sending the first two carriages of the Renfe train down a four-metre slope.

World.title: 2027: No reason to fear INEC will postpone elections – SDP
World.content:
By Henry Umoru

The national leadership of the Social Democratic Party, SDP, has said that there are no reasons to fear that the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, will postpone the 2027 general elections.

Speaking with Vanguard on Wednesday on allegations that INEC was planning to shift the January 16 election, the SDP National Publicity Secretary, Araba Rufus Aiyenigba, said, “For the SDP, there is no justifiable reason to entertain fears that the Commission could be tempted to postpone the scheduled 2027 general elections.

“The public health scare associated with the Ebola reports has been dismissed by the Nigerian Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC), and claims of Ebola being weaponised has been strongly rejected by the health authorities.

“We are yet to have a credible reason to doubt the readiness of INEC for the general polls. The Commission has not given us any reason to be so concerned because there is no sign that surfaced.

“The challenges of security crisis, which could form the basis for election postponement possibility, are yet to be in a dimension of grave concerns.

“It is also necessary to note that the worries that have been variously expressed by the lack of implementation of the provisions of the Electoral Act 2026, particularly delay in the display of voters’ register has been addressed by the Commission with the online upload of the preliminary voters register on its portal.

“While the SDP remains vigilant and will keep its eyes on the ball, the party remains optimistic and positive-minded that nothing will impede the successful conduct of the 2027 general elections.

“It is the nation’s best interests for the elections to hold and be seen to be fair and credibly conducted.”

World.title: Inter leave it late again in Serie A as Bologna sink AC Milan
World.content:
Inter Milan’s French forward #09 Marcus Thuram (R) fights for the ball with Venezia FC’s Croatian midfielder #26 Toma Basic (C) and Venezia FC’s Moroccan defender #25 Redouane Halhal (L) during the Italian Serie A football match between Venezia and Inter Milan at the Pier Luigi Penzo Stadium in Venice, northeastern Italy, on October 28, 2026. (Photo by Stefano Rellandini / AFP)

Inter Milan returned to the Serie A summit with a nervy 2-0 win at bottom side Venezia on Wednesday, while a Samuel Mbangula hat-trick sealed a 4-2 win for Bologna at San Siro to inflict a first league defeat of the season on AC Milan.

Champions Inter drew level with Lazio on 25 points at the top ahead of a hotly anticipated Milan derby meeting with their rivals on Saturday.

Ruben Amorim’s side will go into that game on the back of losing their unbeaten streak after Alphadjo Cisse’s double was not enough to avoid a defeat that left the Rossoneri fifth on 18 points.

Fresh off a pulsating stoppage-time turnaround against Fiorentina on Sunday that marked their fifth comeback win of the season, Inter thought they would have to fight back from behind once again when Lion Lauberbach fired the rock-bottom hosts in front after 29 minutes.

The champions were handed a reprieve when it was ruled out for offside, but had goalkeeper Ivan Provedel to thank for keeping the scores level at the break as he diverted a Lauberbach effort off the bar.

Venezia have picked up just three points all season but looked the likelier to make the breakthrough as Gianluca Busio fired over unmarked from 12 yards before Akor Adams rounded Provedel to score, only for the offside flag to save Inter again.

Last season’s Serie B champions stunned Napoli with a win on new coach Davide Nicola’s debut and another shock result looked possible until they were undone in painful fashion late on.

Matias Moreno and Redouane Halhal diverted dangerous deliveries into their own net in the space of two minutes to ensure Inter returned to the top of the standings and Venezia remained rooted to the bottom.

– Mbangula magic downs Milan –

At San Siro, a lengthy injury list featuring the likes of Adrien Rabiot, Diego Moreira and Mario Gila restricted Amorim’s options for the first midweek round of the season, while the Milan coach left Christian Pulisic and Luka Modric on the bench.

Mbangula, making his full debut for Bologna, swept home the opener inside eight minutes, but the visitors were soon pegged back when an Arthur Theate error gifted Cisse a simple finish.

The Milan teenager struck again in the 27th minute, volleying home a Fikayo Tomori cross, but the game was turned on its head once again in the space of two second-half minutes to stun the San Siro crowd.

The unfortunate Davide Bartesaghi turned a free-kick into his own net before Mbangula struck again with a composed control and finish in the box just after the hour mark.

The 22-year-old then completed a memorable night four minutes from time when he beat Mike Maignan for a third time with a smart finish after Bologna robbed the ball in midfield.

Bologna sealed back-to-back wins for the first time this season to move into 11th place on 11 points.

Elsewhere, Adrian Bernabe had a penalty saved by Maduka Okoye as struggling Parma and Udinese played out a 0-0 draw.

Later on Wednesday, Juventus and Napoli travel to Genoa and Monza respectively.

AFP

World.title: Full list: Ballon d’Or of All Time as Ronaldo emerges winner
World.content:
By Adegboyega Adeleye

Cristiano Ronaldo’s 2008 Ballon d’Or-winning campaign has been voted the best in the history of the prestigious individual football award in a public poll organised to celebrate its 70th anniversary.

The Ballon d’Or announced Ronaldo as the winner of its “Ballon d’Or of All Time” (BOAT) vote on Wednesday, after fans had their say in a poll that opened on October 1 and closed at 23:59 Paris time on October 27. The vote asked fans to choose their favourite Ballon d’Or-winning season.

The result was shared on Wednesday by football transfer journalist Fabrizio Romano via his X page.

Lionel Messi’s 2012 season finished second, with Ronaldo’s 2017 campaign third. Messi’s 2023 season took fourth, while Ronaldo’s 2016 campaign rounded out the top five. The top ten also includes Ronaldo’s 2014 and 2013 seasons, plus Messi’s 2015, 2011 and 2009 campaigns.

Ronaldo’s winning season came in 2007–08 with Manchester United, where he scored 42 goals in all competitions, including 31 in the Premier League and seven in the Champions League. United won both the Premier League and Champions League, with Ronaldo scoring in the final against Chelsea. His league tally earned him the European Golden Shoe, and he went on to win his first Ballon d’Or later that year. The Portuguese legend subsequently won the award four more times, in 2013, 2014, 2016 and 2017, taking his career tally to five.
