World.title: Argentina confirms Bolsonaro crossed via Iguazú before flying to Miami
World.content:
Argentina confirms Bolsonaro crossed via Iguazú before flying to Miami

28th Wednesday, October 2026 - 14:50 UTC Full article

The migration agency’s statement does not say who organised the journey or mention any government involvement

Argentina’s government confirmed that Brazilian Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, defeated in Sunday’s presidential runoff and barred by a court from leaving Brazil, entered Argentina at Puerto Iguazú with his family before flying to the United States on a private plane. Bolsonaro landed on Wednesday morning at Opa-locka Executive Airport in Miami.

“The National Migration Directorate reports that at 22:50 on 27/10, citizens Flavio Nantes Bolsonaro, Fernanda Antunes Figueira Bolsonaro, Carolina Figueira Bolsonaro and Luiza Figueira Bolsonaro entered through the Tancredo Neves International Bridge border crossing in Misiones province,” the agency said in a statement released at 2.01 a.m. on Wednesday. It added that they did so “with valid travel documents and without any legal impediment”. The bridge links Foz do Iguaçu with Puerto Iguazú, and Brazil does not check departures at that crossing, according to the newspaper La Nación.

On Tuesday morning, the migration agency had said it had no record of the senator entering, and presidential spokesman Adrián Ravier denied there had been any asylum request. The crossing took place that night. About 40 minutes later, the family boarded a Gulfstream G400 belonging to Argentine company Baires Fly, which had been waiting at Puerto Iguazú airport since Monday. The plane took off after midnight, made a refuelling stop in Guayaquil, Ecuador, and reached Miami at around 9.20 a.m. on Wednesday, according to Reuters. According to El País, citing the flight manifest, Bolsonaro travelled on his Italian passport, which Judge Alexandre de Moraes had also ordered him to surrender.

The migration agency’s statement does not say who organised the journey or mention any government involvement. Neither the presidency nor Baires Fly immediately responded to press inquiries. Argentine opposition lawmakers had asked the government on Tuesday to clarify whether Bolsonaro used Argentine territory to leave Brazil.

The senator is under investigation at the Supreme Federal Court for alleged money laundering and currency evasion together with a lawyer friend linked to betting companies; both deny wrongdoing. His term ends at the end of the year, when he will lose his parliamentary immunity. The US State Department has said it will grant visas to him and his family.

Javier Milei’s government, which backed Bolsonaro during the campaign, has not congratulated President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva on his re-election. “There will be no statement,” it said.

World.title: Dozens killed as two high-speed trains collide in Spain
World.content:
Dozens killed as two high-speed trains collide in Spain

28th Wednesday, October 2026 - 14:14 UTC Full article

The collision occurred shortly before 9 a.m. at kilometre 118 of the line

At least 68 people were killed on Wednesday when a Renfe AVE high-speed train ran into the back of an Iryo train that was stopped on the Madrid-Seville line near Urda station, in the province of Toledo, according to the president of the Castilla-La Mancha region, Emiliano García-Page. Another 58 people were hospitalised, 15 of them in very serious condition, and authorities fear the death toll will rise.

The collision occurred shortly before 9 a.m. at kilometre 118 of the line. According to García-Page, 24 of the dead were travelling in the lead carriage of the AVE and 44 on the Iryo train, two of whose carriages were destroyed. The Military Emergencies Unit deployed 200 personnel to search for people trapped in the wreckage, and medical helicopters flew the most seriously injured to hospitals in Toledo and Alcázar de San Juan.

Transport Minister Óscar Puente said that at around 8.30 a.m. the LZB control and safety system failed due to a communication fault in three computers, leaving a 63-kilometre stretch without it and automatically stopping six trains. The control centre of rail infrastructure manager Adif at Madrid’s Atocha station then took over and authorised the AVE to resume running normally, despite a red signal and with no speed restriction, according to the minister. The train travelled about 25 kilometres at close to 200 kilometres per hour before the impact. Puente added that the driver of another train corrected the controller, telling him the order should be to proceed “on sight”, at a maximum of 40 kilometres per hour.

“A rear-end collision on the Spanish network is truly implausible,” said Puente, who described the control centre’s decision as “inexplicable” and ruled out resigning for now. The Civil Guard and the Railway Accident Investigation Commission are questioning the operator who was managing traffic.

Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez, who travelled to the scene, declared three days of official mourning. “We will get to the bottom of this and, if there has been negligence, it will be known,” he said. “It is not acceptable for a country like Spain to suffer two high-speed rail accidents in the same year,” he added, referring to the Adamuz crash in Córdoba, which killed 46 people in January. The high-speed line between Madrid and Andalusia remains suspended with no date for reopening, and the train drivers’ union Semaf kept in place a strike called for Thursday over rail safety.

World.title: Adderstone builds on the foundations of hangar success with new Stanley House contract
World.content:
Adderstone builds on the foundations of hangar success with new Stanley House contract

28th Wednesday, October 2026 - 10:28 UTC Full article

M. Wallbank (Managing Director), G. Vatamanu (General Foreman) and Natasha Greenland (General Manager), Adderstone Co. (Falkland Islands) Ltd, outside the newly completed FIGAS hangar, Port Stanley.

Adderstone Construction (Falkland Islands) Limited, part of the Newcastle-headquartered property and construction group, has been awarded a further contract by the Falkland Islands Government, shortly after completing the redevelopment of the FIGAS aircraft hangar in Port Stanley.

The redevelopment gives the islands' air taxi service a hangar built for the long term, keeping communities connected to schools, farms and medical care.

Work is now underway on Adderstone's next Falkland Islands Government contract: upgrading residential amenities at Stanley House. Built in 1878, it is one of Stanley's oldest and most prestigious buildings, and since 1981 it has been where children from the islands' farms and settlements live while they attend secondary school. Children on remote farms,some more than 200 miles from Stanley, are taught at home by travelling teachers until secondary school age. At that point, many move to Stanley and board at Stanley House if their families live too far away to travel each day.

Both projects reflect Adderstone's growth strategy in the Falklands: long-term investment in the infrastructure and buildings that matter to island communities. Stanley House plays a role in island education every bit as vital to daily life as the hangar itself.

Martyn Wallbank, Managing Director of Adderstone's Falkland Islands division, said: “We see our relationship with the Falkland Islands Government as a lasting one, and it rests on doing what we say we'll do. We said we'd deliver on the hangar, and we have. We'll deliver Stanley House in exactly the same way.”

Colin Summers, Director of Public Works, Falkland Islands Government, said: “Adderstone delivered the hangar project on time and to the required standard, and that performance speaks for itself.

“We’re building a longer-term partnership with our delivery partners, including Adderstone, focussed on the essential infrastructure and upgrades that make a genuine difference to life on the islands.

“The FIGAS hangar and Stanley House are examples of that, and we hope there are many more in the future.”

Natasha Greenland, General Manager for Adderstone's Falkland Islands division, added: “I've lived here my whole life, and my family's been here for generations before me.

”That’s why both of these projects matter so much to me - and to families here. They’re about keeping islanders connected to each other, and now, giving children from across the islands a better place to call home while they get their education. That means the world to me, and it’s exactly why we’ll make sure we get this one right too.”

Adderstone's Falkland Islands division is part of a wider Group with operations across the UK and internationally, spanning affordable housing, civil engineering, construction, commercial property management and fit-out.

World.title: Flávio Bolsonaro leaves Brazil despite a court ban and the US will grant him a visa
World.content:
Flávio Bolsonaro leaves Brazil despite a court ban and the US will grant him a visa

28th Wednesday, October 2026 - 09:17 UTC Full article

A State Department official confirmed that visas would be issued for the senator and his family

Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, defeated on Sunday by Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva in the presidential runoff, left Brazil with his wife and two daughters despite a Supreme Federal Court order barring him from leaving the country, and the US State Department confirmed it will grant them visas. According to the newspaper O Globo, he arrived in Miami on Tuesday night.

A State Department official confirmed that visas would be issued for the senator and his family, without specifying the type. Mexican lawyer Simón Levy, who is close to President Donald Trump, said Washington had authorised political asylum, which the US government has not confirmed. His brother Eduardo Bolsonaro lives in Florida, having moved to the United States in 2025, and faces a final arrest warrant in Brazil after being sentenced to four years and two months in prison for coercion in the case against their father.

Judge Alexandre de Moraes had given Bolsonaro 24 hours to surrender his passports as part of an investigation into alleged money laundering through online betting companies, which also involves a lawyer friend of the senator. The deadline expired at 11 a.m. on Tuesday and the Federal Police cancelled his ordinary and diplomatic passports. His exit route has not been officially confirmed. Argentina’s National Migration Directorate, after inspecting a private plane at Iguazú airport highlighted by the press, said its paperwork was in order and that no flight plan including the Bolsonaro family had been submitted. Argentine presidential spokesman Adrián Ravier said there had been no request for asylum.

On Monday, Bolsonaro had said he would hand over his passports and defend himself against “this farce”, and that his place was “beside the Brazilian people”. That same day, Supreme Court Judge Flávio Dino ordered the Federal Police to investigate possible foreign financing of his campaign, following complaints about contributions from Rockbridge Network, a network of US conservative donors founded by Vice President JD Vance, and alleged manipulation of social media algorithms. The senator is also under investigation over his links with banker Daniel Vorcaro, jailed over the Banco Master case.

“A citizen who sneaks out of his country must owe something. Leaving Brazil is shameful,” Lula said on Tuesday at a celebration of his 81st birthday. “He could have stayed here and shown that the accusations were not true,” he added.

Bolsonaro never formally recognised his defeat, although his Liberal Party accepted the result. His father, Jair Bolsonaro, also travelled to Florida after losing the 2022 election, two days before Lula’s inauguration, and stayed there until late March 2023. Lula will begin his fourth term on January 5, 2027.

World.title: Trump suggests Venezuela become the 51st US state and elect a governor
World.content:
Trump suggests Venezuela become the 51st US state and elect a governor

28th Wednesday, October 2026 - 03:36 UTC Full article

“We’re bringing out a lot of oil for ourselves, a lot. It will become a prosperous country, and who knows? Maybe someday soon it will become a prosperous 51st state. That’s possible,” Trump said

US President Donald Trump suggested on Tuesday that Venezuela become the 51st US state and that its citizens elect a governor instead of a president, at a rally at the port of Corpus Christi, Texas, where he announced the arrival of the first shipment of one million barrels of Venezuelan oil obtained under an agreement between Washington and Caracas.

“We’re bringing out a lot of oil for ourselves, a lot. It will become a prosperous country, and who knows? Maybe someday soon it will become a prosperous 51st state. That’s possible,” Trump said, standing beside an oil tanker at an event backing Republican candidates a week before the November 3 midterm elections. “Let’s make it. Let’s make it the 51st state. And instead of a president, we’ll have an election for a governor. How about that? You know, they have a lot of oil.”

The president thanked Venezuela for a relationship he described as “very, very good” and presented the shipment as “a historic win that gives us control over a massive part of the world’s oil supply”. The crude, which Trump described as free, will be refined in Texas, including in Corpus Christi. “Billions and billions of dollars are now being invested by the biggest oil companies,” he added.

It is not the first time Trump has raised annexing Venezuela. In February he said it could become the 53rd state, after Canada and Greenland, and in August he shared a map of the country in the colours of the US flag with the caption “51st state”. Acting President Delcy Rodríguez has rejected the idea on several occasions; in July she said Venezuela has more than two centuries of sovereignty.

The remarks come amid close cooperation between the two governments. After the US military operation on January 3 that removed Nicolás Maduro from power, now jailed and on trial in New York, Washington recognised Rodríguez’s government, lifted sanctions on her and her brother, National Assembly President Jorge Rodríguez, and in August sealed an oil agreement giving it majority control over a significant share of Venezuela’s reserves. The State Department has said that under the roadmap negotiated with the opposition, Rodríguez should leave the presidency vacant in 2027, although the presidential election still has no date.

The rally came two days after opposition leader María Corina Machado returned to Venezuela after nearly ten months abroad. Trump said he hoped Machado “is safe”, and Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Washington had urged Rodríguez to allow her return. The acting president called the opposition leader’s arrival a “show”.

World.title: Latin America’s energy inflation reaches its highest level in a year
World.content:
Latin America’s energy inflation reaches its highest level in a year

28th Wednesday, October 2026 - 03:30 UTC Full article

The study, based on data from the statistics institutes and central banks of member countries, shows energy inflation exceeded the previous high for the period, 8.03% in June

Annual energy inflation in Latin America and the Caribbean accelerated to 8.33% in August, its highest level in twelve months, and pressure on fuel prices continued in September and October, when diesel prices matched petrol for the first time, according to a report by the Latin American Energy Organization (OLADE) published by the Energy Report website.

The study, based on data from the statistics institutes and central banks of member countries, shows energy inflation exceeded the previous high for the period, 8.03% in June. Overall inflation in the region rose from 4.17% in July to 4.43% in August. The report links the acceleration to the resumption of hostilities between Iran and the United States in July, after a fragile ceasefire in June.

Diesel has risen faster than petrol. In August, its regional average price rose 2.5% to US$1.31 per litre, almost four times the increase in petrol, which rose 0.6% to US$1.38. In October, both fuels reached US$1.41 per litre, the highest level of the year. Since February, diesel has risen 26% compared with 18% for petrol, and the report expects it could overtake petrol in the coming weeks. Its rising cost has a particular impact on freight and passenger transport, farm machinery and the distribution of goods.

WTI crude averaged US$83.90 per barrel in August, US$97.31 in September and around US$98.29 in October. The report warns that the pass-through of crude prices to fuel is asymmetric: international increases are passed on quickly, while decreases are reflected with a delay or only partially, due to inventories, retail margins, taxes, subsidies and local price stabilisation mechanisms.

World.title: Argentina: opposition asks Milei to clarify whether Bolsonaro left Brazil through the country
World.content:
Argentina: opposition asks Milei to clarify whether Bolsonaro left Brazil through the country

28th Wednesday, October 2026 - 03:20 UTC Full article

Milei backed Bolsonaro during the campaign and repeatedly called Lula a “thief” and a “jailbird”

Argentine opposition lawmakers on Tuesday demanded that Javier Milei’s government report whether Brazilian Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, who left Brazil despite a court ban and travelled to the United States after his election defeat, crossed through Argentine territory. The National Migration Directorate said it has no record of the senator entering the country.

“There is no record of any entry by Flávio Bolsonaro into the Argentine Republic,” the agency said in a statement. It explained that after press reports of a private plane at Puerto Iguazú airport, in the Triple Frontier area with Brazil and Paraguay, it inspected the aircraft and its crew and “found that the company’s paperwork is in order and no flight plan including the Bolsonaro family was submitted”. Presidential spokesman Adrián Ravier said there had been “no request for asylum”. The route by which Bolsonaro left Brazil has not been officially confirmed.

Peronist Senator Juliana Di Tullio said the government, through Interior Minister Diego Santilli, “must explain whether Bolsonaro used our border and our territory to escape from Brazil”. Left Front deputy Myriam Bregman called on the authorities to clarify “whether Bolsonaro, Milei’s fugitive friend, passed through Argentina”. Socialist deputy Esteban Paulón filed a formal request for information in the Chamber of Deputies asking the executive to state whether there are records of the senator’s entry or exit and whether the country received notice of the court restrictions placed on him.

Milei backed Bolsonaro during the campaign and repeatedly called Lula a “thief” and a “jailbird”, prompting Brazil to recall its ambassador in Buenos Aires for consultations in July. The Argentine government has not congratulated the Brazilian president on his re-election and, according to El País, confirmed it will issue no official statement on the result.

The case revives a precedent that has already strained bilateral relations: in recent years, dozens of people charged or convicted over the January 8, 2023 storming of the seats of the three branches of government in Brasília have settled in Argentina, according to media in both countries.

World.content:
All stories in El Jalapeño are satire and not real news. Check out the original articles here and here.

TULUM, Quintana Roo — In a bold display of logistical agility, ride-hailing giant Uber announced Friday that it will step in to replace canceled commercial airline routes to Tulum by dispatching drivers in 2018 Nissan Versas for direct, 22-hour interstate road trips from the United States.

The move comes after major carriers, including American Airlines, Aeroméxico and Volaris, announced reductions or pauses in service to Felipe Carrillo Puerto International Airport, leaving thousands of vacationers searching for alternative flight arrangements to the Quintana Roo resort town.

Under the company’s newly launched “UberLongHaul” tier, passengers stranded in hub cities like Miami, Charlotte or Atlanta can bypass commercial aviation entirely and hail a subcompact sedan straight to their beachside hotel lobby. The app automatically calculates toll fees, international border wait times and recommended driver shifts along the 1,400-mile highway route.

“While airlines are constrained by pilot shortages and complex airspace logistics, our driver-partners remain completely nimble,” said Uber regional strategy director Carlos Mendoza. “If a traveler in Florida needs to reach a wellness retreat in Quintana Roo, they shouldn’t be limited by flight schedules. They can simply tap a button and settle into a comfortable subcompact ride through a dozen or so picturesque states in the U.S. and Mexico.”

To accommodate long-haul passengers unused to multi-day highway commutes, participating drivers will provide onboard amenities including room-temperature bottled water, periodic air conditioning and head and neck pillows for sleeping.

Transportation experts have praised the initiative as a practical response to shifts in international transit patterns, noting that while jetliners face strict operational hurdles, a compact sedan can easily adapt to evolving travel demands provided passengers maintain patience through the long journey.

State tourism officials expressed optimism about the service integration, calling it a testament to modern flexibility. “Whether visitors arrive via direct flight or a multi-day highway ride-share, the important thing is that they get here,” said regional transit consultant Maria Gutierrez.

World.title: Mexico City opens investigation into fatal poisoning of dogs in Condesa
World.content:
Suspected poison hidden inside sausage at Parque España in Mexico City might have killed at least three dogs Tuesday, prompting a criminal investigation and warnings for pet owners in the capital’s Condesa neighborhood.

The Mexico City Attorney General’s Office opened an animal cruelty investigation after dogs became ill following walks in the 105-year-old park.

Residents reported four deaths, according to Uno TV, while Cuauhtémoc borough Mayor Alessandra Rojo de la Vega reported at least three, Infobae reported.

Police found a piece of longaniza, a seasoned sausage, containing a blue pill with white powder inside, La Crónica reported. However, authorities had not publicly identified the substance or established whether it was linked to the dogs’ illnesses.

Residents also reported finding suspected poisoned meat one block from Parque España, at the intersection of Avenida Veracruz and Calle Atlixco, La Crónica reported.

Excélsior reported that five dogs arrived at the Vetme veterinary hospital suffering from seizures, prompting staff to alert authorities. Three died and two remained hospitalized.

Among those that died was Rufián, a 4-year-old Irish setter-golden retriever mix.

“Three minutes after he arrived home, he started convulsing,” said Sofía Suárez, the dog’s owner and the mother of a 2-year-old.

“How am I going to tell my daughter that she doesn’t have a dog anymore? We’d go to the park every morning and every afternoon,” she said.

Two other dogs, a Belgian shepherd named Kiara and a small-breed dog named Siberia, remained hospitalized, Excélsior reported.

Their owner, Brenda Gómez Magaña, told the newspaper that blue capsules were recovered during a stomach lavage. Kiara appeared to be improving, while Siberia remained in serious condition.

Rojo de la Vega requested a review of surveillance footage and announced legal assistance for families filing complaints.

Investigators were collecting owners’ statements, examining evidence and seeking help from veterinary specialists. Excélsior reported Tuesday evening that authorities had collected nine pieces of evidence suspected of containing poison.

A neighborhood representative said the park would remain open, but its popular dog run and children’s areas would close pending cleanup. Residents wanted the entire park cleaned once prosecutors authorized the work.

Authorities began preventive patrols. Rojo de la Vega urged visitors to Parque España and nearby Parque México to prevent pets from eating anything off the ground and report information to investigators.

With reports from Infobae, Uno TV, Excélsior and La Crónica

World.title: Navy kills cartel operator Jesús ‘Chuy’ González, wanted by the US for $5M
World.content:
Jesús “Chuy” González Peñuelas, an alleged leader of the Guasave Cartel, is believed to have been killed during a clash with Mexican Navy personnel in Sinaloa on Monday, federal authorities said.

The death of González — a 56-year-old alleged drug trafficker who was wanted in the United States — was first reported by media outlets in Sinaloa.

In a social media post on Wednesday, the Navy Ministry (SEMAR) said that its personnel, in coordination with federal Security Ministry agents, “repelled an armed attack” near the community of Alfredo V. Bonfil, located in the municipality of Sinaloa in the state of the same name.

Personal naval de la @SEMAR_mx en coordinación con @SSPCMexico, repelió una agresión armada en inmediaciones de Alfredo V. Bonfil, #Sinaloa. Esta acción derivó de trabajos de inteligencia naval y como resultado se aseguraron 4 vehículos con reporte de robo, 3 armas largas, cargadores y municiones. Durante el enfrentamiento fallecieron 2 personas, cuya identidad podría corresponder a Jesús “N” (a) Chuy Peñuelas operador de 2do orden, solo por debajo de Fausto Isidro Meza Flores (a) Chapo Isidro, líder del Cartel de Guasave y Cesáreo “N”, quedando pendiente la confirmación pericial. Los indicios quedaron a disposición de la @FGRMexico para las investigaciones correspondientes. #Marina refrenda su compromiso de contribuir a la seguridad de la población, mediante la coordinación interinstitucional, con apego al marco legal y respeto a los derechos humanos. — SEMAR México (@SEMAR_mx) October 28, 2026

SEMAR said that two people died during the confrontation, adding that their “identities may correspond to” González and a man identified as Cesáreo “N”.

In a separate social media post, federal Security Minister Omar García Harfuch said that, “according to the available information,” González was one of the two people killed in the clash with military personnel on Monday.

SEMAR said that “expert confirmation” that González and Cesáreo “N” were the two people killed was “pending.”

Cesáreo “N” was identified in media reports as Cesáreo Peñuelas Ruiz, aka “El Profe” (The Teacher). He was reportedly González’s uncle.

The Navy Ministry said that its operation in the municipality of Sinaloa on Monday “stemmed from naval intelligence work.”

During the operation, four vehicles reported as stolen, three long guns, magazines and ammunition were seized, SEMAR said.

Who was Jesús ‘Chuy’ González Peñuelas?

According to SEMAR, González was the Guasave Cartel’s second-in-command, below only Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, aka “Chapo Isidro.”

The Guasave Cartel is also known as the Meza Flores Organization and Los Mazaltecos. It is based in the municipality of Guasave in northern Sinaloa.

While SEMAR and García Harfuch said on Wednesday that Gonzalez was a member of the Guasave Cartel, U.S. authorities have accused him of running his own drug trafficking organization.

In January 2024, the U.S. Department of State announced a reward of up to US $5 million for information leading to the arrest and/or conviction of González, saying at the time that he “reportedly leads an independent methamphetamine, marijuana, heroin, and cocaine distribution and production organization.”

The State Department noted that González had been indicted on international narcotics charges in the District of Colorado and the Southern District of California.

The U.S. Department of the Treasury said in May 2021 that González and his drug trafficking organization were “among the largest sources of raw opium gum and heroin in northern Mexico, and increasingly are a major distributor of fentanyl to U.S. markets.”

At that time, Treasury’s Office of Foreign Assets Control designated González and his drug trafficking organization as “significant foreign narcotics traffickers pursuant to the Foreign Narcotics Kingpin Designation Act.”

The Department of the Treasury said that González oversaw “multiple heroin processing laboratories in Sinaloa” and that “the upper echelons” of his drug trafficking organization (DTO) hierarchy consisted of his family members.

“The González Peñuelas DTO cooperates with other DTOs within Mexico, including acting as an enforcement arm for the various Mexican DTO’s trafficking routes, and is aligned with Mexican drug kingpins Fausto Isidro Meza Flores and Rafael Caro Quintero, both of whom are subject to Treasury sanctions,” the department said on May 12, 2021.

With reports from Río Doce, EFE and El Financiero

World.title: Tropical Storm Vance heads toward Sinaloa, bringing more heavy rainfall to northwest Mexico
World.content:
Tropical Storm Vance continues to move northward off the coast of western Mexico and is projected to turn toward the coast of Sinaloa, where it could make landfall by the end of this week.

The U.S. National Hurricane Center forecasts that Vance will lose strength and become a post-tropical remnant low on Thursday, potentially approaching Sinaloa between Thursday and Friday. Landfall as a tropical storm is unlikely.

According to the National Meteorological Service, as of 12 p.m. today, Vance was located approximately 365 kilometers west-southwest of Cabo Corrientes, Jalisco, and 390 kilometers west-southwest of Punta Mita, Nayarit. The storm had sustained winds of 65 kilometers per hour, with gusts reaching up to 85 kilometers per hour and was heading north at a speed of 17 kilometers per hour.

A las 12:00h, la #TormentaTropical #Vance se localiza a 365 km al oeste-suroeste de Cabo Corrientes, #Jalisco, con vientos máximos sostenidos de 65 km/h y rachas de 85 km/h. Se desplaza hacia el nor-noroeste a 17 km/h. ⚠️ Para las próximas 24 horas se pronostican lluvias muy fuertes con puntuales intensas (75 a 150 mm) en Baja California Sur, Sinaloa, Nayarit, Jalisco y Durango. En Colima, lluvias puntuales fuertes (25 a 50 mm). 🌬️ En la costa de Jalisco se esperan vientos de 30 a 40 km/h con rachas de 50 a 70 km/h y 🌊 oleaje de 2.5 a 3.5 metros. En las costas de Baja California Sur, Sinaloa, Nayarit y Colima, oleaje de 1.5 a 2.5 metros. 📲 Consulta solo fuentes oficiales: @conagua_clima y @CNPC_MX. — Coordinación Nacional de Protección Civil (@CNPC_MX) October 28, 2026

Vance is expected to cause heavy rain across Mexico’s western states.

On Wednesday, rainfall totals of 75 to 150 millimeters are expected in central and southern Sinaloa, Nayarit, Durango, the southern tip of Baja California Sur and the coast of Jalisco.

The coastlines of Baja California Sur, Sinaloa, Nayarit and Colima could get hit with sustained winds of 20 to 30 kilometers per hour with gusts of 40 to 60 kilometers per hour and waves of 1.5 to 2.5 meters, while Jalisco could see waves of up to 3.5 meters.

In Baja California Sur, the Public Education Ministry (SEP) suspended all school activities for Wednesday in San José del Cabo and Cabo San Lucas. This suspension applies to all public and private educational institutions at every level.

Given the potential for rivers and streams to swell, authorities warned residents in affected states to avoid crossing watercourses or flooded areas, stay alert to weather advisories and follow the instructions provided by Civil Protection authorities.

With reports from López Dóriga

World.title: Jalisco governor details US $1.3B investment in Guadalajara’s water infrastructure: Wednesday’s mañanera recapped
World.content:
Listen to this article

Sheinbaum’s mañanera in 60 seconds

💧 Lemus announces “historic agreement” on Guadalajara water: Jalisco Governor Pablo Lemus said the federal and state governments will invest 25 billion pesos (US $1.33 billion) in water infrastructure for the Guadalajara metropolitan area. The plan includes the construction of two new aqueducts: one from Lake Chapala (42 kilometers) to Guadalajara and one from the Calderón Reservoir to the San Gaspar treatment plant (31 kilometers). The federal government will contribute 14.5 billion pesos and Jalisco 10.2 billion pesos, with no new debt, privatization or water rate increases. Lemus said work “could” start next year and that the aqueducts should be finished by the end of 2028.

Lemus said work “could” start next year and that the aqueducts should be finished by the end of 2028. 🇲🇽🇺🇸 Sheinbaum says Mexico-U.S. trade talks have made “a lot” of progress: The president said Economy Minister Marcelo Ebrard spoke this week with U.S. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick about whether a bilateral deal is “possible” before next Tuesday’s U.S. midterm elections. She conceded there are still unresolved issues, saying Mexico wants a “significant reduction” of U.S. Section 232 tariffs on vehicles, steel and aluminum.

The president said Economy Minister Marcelo Ebrard spoke this week with U.S. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick about whether a bilateral deal is “possible” before next Tuesday’s U.S. midterm elections. She conceded there are still unresolved issues, saying Mexico wants a “significant reduction” of U.S. Section 232 tariffs on vehicles, steel and aluminum. 🇪🇸 Sheinbaum expresses solidarity with Spain after deadly train crash: Asked about the high-speed train collision near Toledo, which killed at least 68 people and injured more than 50, Sheinbaum said Mexico stands ready to help. She said she would ask Foreign Affairs Minister Roberto Velasco whether any Mexicans were affected.

Why today’s mañanera matters

The centerpiece of President Claudia Sheinbaum’s Wednesday morning press conference was the announcement of a plan to address the long-running problem of water contamination in the metropolitan area of Guadalajara, Jalisco.

Jalisco Governor Pablo Lemus said that the federal and state governments will contribute funds to the plan, which includes the construction of two new aqueducts.

Today’s announcement comes after thousands of Guadalajara residents demanded clean tap water at large protest marches earlier this month.

Also of note at today’s mañanera were Sheinbaum’s remarks about Mexico’s trade negotiations with the United States and her expression of solidarity with the people of Spain, where a train accident killed at least 68 people on Wednesday.

Jalisco governor announces ‘historic agreement’ to address water problems in Guadalajara

Lemus declared that it was “a historic day” for the metropolitan area of Guadalajara, Jalisco and “all of Mexico” given that the Jalisco and federal governments had reached “a historic agreement” to together invest 25 billion pesos (US $1.33 billion) in “the infrastructure necessary to supply quality water to families in the metropolitan area of Guadalajara.”

“The historic legacy that the federal government and the Jalisco government will leave will be to have solved the water problem for the next generations,” he said.

#Mañanera Lemus informó que Jalisco construirá una nueva red de colectores para evitar que el agua que viene de Chapala se contamine en la presa Las Pintas. Además, detectaron 150 descargas irregulares en el canal, que están siendo clausuradas, y sus responsables serán sancionados. 📹 Gobierno federal

https://t.co/uhCGj87YOO — REFORMA (@Reforma) October 28, 2026

As a result of the agreement, the federal government will build new aqueducts “for the people of Jalisco,” Lemus said.

He noted that the aqueducts will run between Lake Chapala and Guadalajara, and between the Calderón Reservoir and the San Gaspar water treatment plant, located in the metropolitan area of the state capital.

Lemus said that work on the new aqueducts “could” start next year. He said that the aqueducts are expected to be finished at the end of 2028.

Lemus told reporters that Guadalajara receives 60% of its water supply from Lake Chapala and a “significant part” of that water reaches the state capital via “an open canal built 70 years ago.”

That canal, he said, is “exposed to discharges of wastewater.”

“With the new aqueduct we will take less water from Chapala … and we’ll be able to use 100% of that water without it being contaminated in the journey [to Guadalajara] and without waste due to leaks or evaporation,” Lemus said.

The governor noted that the federal government will contribute 14.5 billion pesos to the 25-billion-peso water infrastructure plan — which includes various projects to complement the new aqueducts — while the Jalisco government will provide 10.2 billion pesos.

He said the investment will ensure that all residents of the metropolitan area of Guadalajara have clean water in the near future.

Lemus said that the state and federal money will be made available through “budget adjustments.”

“There will be no debt, … there will be no privatization and a very important thing is that there won’t be increases to water rates for the metropolitan area of Guadalajara,” he said.

According to information presented by National Water Commission chief Efraín Morales, the federal government will invest 9.3 billion pesos in the 42-kilometer-long aqueduct between Chapala and Guadalajara and 5.2 billion pesos in the 31-kilometer-long Calderón-San Gaspar aqueduct.

Could Mexico and the US reach a trade deal before the US midterms?

Sheinbaum told reporters that Economy Minister Marcelo Ebrard spoke to U.S. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick about trade issues earlier this week. She said the officials looked at whether it was “possible” to reach a bilateral agreement before the U.S. midterm elections next Tuesday.

Sheinbaum said that a lot of progress has been made in Mexico’s trade talks with the U.S., but conceded that “there are still issues on which we haven’t yet reached an agreement.”

“We want a significant reduction of the [United States’ Section] 232 tariffs on vehicles, steel and aluminum,” she said.

“… We haven’t yet reached [an agreement on] what we consider important for Mexico, but there is very good dialogue, very good progress and a very good atmosphere in the communication,” Sheinbaum said.

Mexico and the United States have been seeking to resolve a range of trade-related issues following the U.S. government’s decision in July not to renew the USMCA free trade pact for an additional 16 years.

Both Sheinbaum and U.S. President Donald Trump said last week that Mexico and the U.S. were “very close” to reaching a deal.

Sheinbaum expresses ‘solidarity’ with the people of Spain after rail disaster near Toledo

A reporter asked the president about the deadly train crash near the central Spanish city of Toledo.

Sheinbaum expressed “solidarity” with the people of Spain and said that Mexico stood ready to help.

Video shows the immediate aftermath of a deadly high-speed train collision in central Spain on Wednesday that killed at least 64 people and injured 80 others, authorities said. The crash occurred in the province of Toledo when a high-speed train slammed into the back of another train that had stopped, derailing two cars. Both trains were traveling from Madrid to Seville, carrying a combined 544 passengers. The cause of the crash remains unknown. — CBS News (@CBSNews) October 28, 2026

As of 12 p.m. Mexico City time on Wednesday, 68 people were confirmed to have been killed in the accident, while more than 50 people were reported injured. The crash occurred when a high-speed train slammed into the rear of another train that had stopped on the tracks.

Sheinbaum said she heard about the crash just before she began her Wednesday morning press conference. She said she would ask Foreign Affairs Minister Roberto Velasco whether any Mexicans were affected.

The Ministry of Foreign Affairs expressed its condolences to the people and government of Spain in a social media post, but didn’t say whether any Mexicans had been killed or injured in the crash.

By Mexico News Daily chief staff writer Peter Davies (peter.davies@mexiconewsdaily.com)

World.title: MND Local Puerto Vallarta: High season kicks off with Día de Muertos, artisan markets, PGA Tour and HEAT Latin Music Awards
World.content:
High season is around the corner, and Puerto Vallarta is gearing up to welcome visitors from the north. Tianguis, or outdoor artisan markets, are opening this week; entertainment venues are announcing their winter lineups, and Avenida México on the Malecón just got a facelift.

The season kicks off with Día de Muertos — Mexico’s colorful and joyful tribute to departed souls; the HEAT Latin Music Awards; and a Professional Golf Association (PGA) tournament at VidantaWorld.

Read on and mark your calendars with fun things to do only available during high season.

Día de Muertos

Puerto Vallarta will put on another epic Día de Muertos celebration this year with its monumental Catrina on the Malecón (although this year Vallarta will lose its “tallest Catrina in the world” Guinness World Record to Mexico City) and events planned throughout the historic city center from Oct. 28 to Nov. 2.

Highlights include 50 large-scale Catrinas displayed along the Malecón, a lighted boat parade to pay homage to departed fishermen, ballet folklórico presentations at Los Arcos, live mariachi at Plaza de Armas, and a grand parade of Catrinas, Catrines and musicians from the municipal cemetery to the Los Muertos beach pier.

All events are free and open to the public. I recommend getting downtown before sunset if you are driving or taking public transport. Last year, we waited until nightfall, and it took over an hour to drive from the marina to the Malecón, just 8 kilometers away. It’s a beautiful celebration you don’t want to miss.

Artisan market openings

Local artisans and food vendors are busy making, baking and crafting to prepare for Vallarta’s many artisanal tianguis — or outdoor markets — that run during high season. The three main markets are the La Cruz Market on Sundays in Nuevo Vallarta, the Thursday night market at Marina Vallarta, and the Olas Altas Farmers Market on Saturdays in the Romantic Zone.

Visitors can fill their shopping bags with locally made treats, jewelry, artwork and more nearly every day of the week. We’ve made the Thursday night Marina Vallarta market part of our winter dining routine. Some of our favorite goodies are the BBQ pork sandwiches, Oaxacan (banana leaf-wrapped) tamales, baklava, peanut brittle and tamarindo-infused ginger beer. We also love the live entertainment and unique artwork you can find at the La Cruz market.

The Marina Vallarta market opens Thursday, Oct. 29; La Cruz Market on Sunday, Nov. 1; and Olas Altas Farmers Market on Saturday, Nov. 7. Come prepared to shop and eat well!

VidantaWorld Mexico Open 2026

Professional golfers from around the world will compete for a purse of US $6 million at the Mexico Open 2026. The tournament takes place Oct. 26 to Nov. 1 at the VidantaWorld resort in Nuevo Vallarta.

The first Mexico Open was held in 1944 at the Chapultepec Golf Club outside of Mexico City. After 1960, the tournament traveled to different courses around the country. It moved to the VidantaWorld course in Nuevo Vallarta in 2022 when it became an official PGA Tour event. The competition is broadcast internationally and has put Puerto Vallarta and Nuevo Vallarta on the map for golf fans worldwide.

Among the players competing this year are last year’s Mexico Open champion Brian Campbell, along with previous tournament champ Tony Finau and other top-ranked players such as Wyndham Clark, Lucas Glover and Ben Griffin. Also joining the 120 pros on the course will be local Mexican champs Álvaro Ortiz, Omar Morales and Santiago de la Fuente.

The four-day tournament coincides with the opening of the resort’s Bon theme park on Oct. 24 and a Robbie Williams concert on Oct. 27. Tournament tickets are available on FeverUp, or you can catch it streaming online on the Golf Channel.

HEAT Latin Music Awards

Puerto Vallarta will host the 11th annual HEAT Latin Music Awards gala this year, making it the first Mexican city to do so. The awards ceremony takes place on Nov. 5 at the Puerto Vallarta International Convention Center and caps off a week of art, music and cultural performances in Jalisco.

View this post on Instagram A post shared by HEAT LATIN MUSIC AWARDS (@lospremiosheat)

The HEAT awards honor musicians from across Latin America, with categories for best salsa, tropical and Dominican artist, plus a new category this year for best regional Mexican artist. Since Sept. 24, fans have been voting for their favorite artists via the LosHeatTV mobile app.

Leading the list of nominees is Colombian singer Karol G, nominated for 10 awards including best female artist, best urban artist, album of the year (for “Tropicoqueta”) and best viral song (“Bby WOW”), among others. Bad Bunny follows with nine nominations, and Carlos Rivera and Shakira with seven nominations each.

Smaller than the industry-led Latin Grammys and Billboard Latin Music Awards, the HEAT awards are voted on by fans and focused on more regional Latin American music and digital creators.

So although the high season is around the corner, the temperatures (and music) are still hot in Puerto Vallarta.

And if the HEAT awards get you longing for live Latin and Mexican music, in the next events roundup I’ll feature some of the best places in Vallarta to see local musicians.

Debbie Slobe is a writer and communications strategist based in Puerto Vallarta, Jalisco. She blogs at Mexpatmama.com and is a senior program director at Resource Media. Find her on Instagram and Facebook.

World.title: Protesters file complaints with Attorney General’s Office alleging torture at hands of Jalisco state police officers
World.content:
“I stopped breathing because they were suffocating me.”

“They subdued me with water, and four or five men came over and grabbed me by each of my limbs and by my hair. Then they said all sorts of things to me: ‘You fucking bitch, you whore, you don’t know what’s going to happen to you.'”

Those are the words of two women who allege they were tortured by Jalisco state police officers during an Oct. 11 protest in Guadalajara to demand clean tap water.

Adriana Gabriela Arreola Dueñas, a lawyer and leader of a collective called “Access to Health, Justice and Education,” and Daniela Álvarez Zepeda, a medical doctor, are among around 10 people who have filed complaints with the Federal Attorney General’s Office (FGR) alleging that they were tortured and unjustly detained by police in Guadalajara on Oct. 11.

The two women recounted their traumatic experiences at a press conference on Monday. Their allegations, and those made by other protesters, are under investigation by the Jalisco Attorney General’s Office (FGE). The FGR has not publicly said whether it has commenced its own investigation.

In addition to the FGE, the National Human Rights Commission is investigating the events in Guadalajara on Oct. 11. It said in a statement that it was investigating “possible violations of human rights during a protest for access to potable water in Guadalajara,” where water contamination is a long-running problem.

Police used tear gas and water cannons against protesters gathered outside Casa Jalisco, the official residence of Jalisco Governor Pablo Lemus, a representative of the Citizens Movement party. Officers are also alleged to have physically and verbally abused demonstrators. Dozens of people were hurt and at least 39 people were arrested during the protest.

Arreola alleges she was suffocated, partially stripped and kicked in the head

Arreola filed a complaint with the FGR on Oct. 14. She alleges that both she and her 19-year-old daughter were victims of police brutality on Oct. 11.

On Monday, Arreola said that three female police officers grabbed her while she was protesting at Casa Jalisco. She said the officers attacked her, verbally abused her and told her to shut her “snout.”

Arreola said that officers pulled down her pants within the grounds of Casa Jalisco, leaving her semi-naked. She said that one officer kicked her back while she lay on the ground partially clothed. Arreola also said that officers used her own scarf to tie her hands together behind her back. She said police yanked her by her hands to force her to stand up, injuring her shoulders in the process.

Arreola also said that officers sat and jumped on her back, leaving her breathless.

“I stopped breathing because they were suffocating me,” she said.

Arreola also said that a person dressed in civilian clothing — possibly a plainclothes police officer — kicked her in the head.

Álvarez: ‘All we wanted was clean water’

Álvarez, the doctor, said Monday that she was “grabbed” by police officers after she was hit with a water cannon outside Casa Jalisco on Oct. 11. Like Arreola, she said she was subjected to verbal abuse.

Álvarez, who filed a complaint with the FGR on Oct. 15, said she suffered a neck strain and bruises during her violent arrest. She also said that officers took her phone and broke her bag.

Álvarez said that she and other protesters weren’t trying to make any political point when they took to the streets to protest on Oct. 11.

“All we wanted was clean water,” she said.

Detention inside the Casa Jalisco compound

Both Álvarez and Arreola said they were held in a small room inside the Casa Jalisco compound after they were detained. All told, around 40 people — some with bloody injuries — were allegedly held in the room for hours.

During the protesters’ detention, police officers allegedly threatened to “disappear them.” One officer allegedly said they would be taken to a place “where no one will find them.”

Álvarez said that one young woman began to “convulse” inside the “five by five meter” room.

“As a doctor, I tried to go over to her, at least to put her in a safe position. [But] they wouldn’t let me approach,” she said.

Álvarez said that paramedics arrived to assist her, but the woman started convulsing again.

“Police said she was faking, they laughed at her,” she said.

José Francisco Salazar González, a lawyer and academic at the University of Guadalajara, described the small room inside the Casa Jalisco precinct as a “torture center” where there was a “suspension” of detainees’ human rights.

Governor Lemus was apparently not at his official residence when the acts of police brutality and torture were allegedly committed.

Transfer to an FGE lockup

Arreola and Álvarez said that they and other detained protesters were eventually transferred to a Jalisco Attorney General’s Office facility where they were placed in cells. They said they were held in cold conditions and had no access to their phones.

It was not until Tuesday, Oct. 13, that Lemus announced that all the people detained during the protest on Oct. 11 had been released.

He conceded that authorities made “serious mistakes” during the protest. He said those mistakes “must be investigated and punished.”

Arreola, Álvarez and others are calling for Lemus and Jalisco Security Minister Juan Pablo Hernández González to be investigated.

‘It wasn’t me’: Hernández denies he gave an order to use force against protesters

Asked last Thursday who gave police the order to use force against protesters at Casa Jalisco, Hernández responded, “Yo no fui” (It wasn’t me).

” … We have several statements from police officers and commanders; three of the latter are involved, they’ll probably receive a sanction,” the security minister said.

Roberto Alarcón Estrada, the Jalisco government’s strategic security coordinator, told reporters that the names of police commanders who issued orders to use force against protesters couldn’t be disclosed. He said that the disclosure of their names could place them at risk of retaliation by protesters detained on Oct. 11 and/or their family members.

For his part, Jalisco Attorney General Salvador González de los Santos said that the FGE didn’t send any personnel to assist the police operation during the Oct. 11 protest in Guadalajara. The news magazine Proceso reported that his statement was “relevant” given that there have been allegations that officers dressed in civilian clothing were present during the police “intervention” at Casa Jalisco.

On repeated occasions, President Claudia Sheinbaum has denounced the alleged torture committed by police in Guadalajara on Oct. 11.

“How is it possible that in 2026, there is still torture of young people by police?” she remarked at her morning press conference on Oct. 14.

“… We, who came from the fight against [government] repression, cannot allow there to be police forces in Mexico that repress and torture,” Sheinbaum said.

With reports from Proceso and La Jornada

World.title: With Day of the Dead less than a week away, Mexico City’s cempasúchil production hits record heights
World.content:
The Mexico City area has achieved a record production of 10 million cempasúchil plants — a Mexican variety of marigold that is important for Day of the Dead celebrations — marking a 53.8% increase over last year’s cultivation figure, Mayor Clara Brugada announced last week.

The bright orange flowers were grown by producers on chinampas (artificial islands) in the southern Xochimilco borough of the capital, with support from the city government, which contributed over 8 million pesos (US $428,100) to directly support 597 producers.

The government provided technical assistance, distributed pots, compost and seeds, and carried out work to prepare cultivation areas, rehabilitate roads and provide harvesting facilities.

Growing flowers each year provides vital revenue to rural communities and contributes to the preservation of chinampa gardens and conservation land.

People are advised to purchase plants with a Green Seal, an image indicating that the cempasúchil flowers were grown on conservation land in Mexico City and guaranteeing sustainable production. The flowers are being sold in all 16 boroughs of Mexico City, including markets in Xochimilco, with plants priced at 15 to 30 pesos (US 80 cents to $1.60).

Xochimilco’s head of government, Cirse Camacho, thanked the Mexico City government for its support of the district’s producers, and emphasized the importance of the contribution to the recovery of the region’s agricultural sector following flood damage.

Mayor Brugada also highlighted the free cultural events being held across the city over Día de Muertos (Day of the Dead) weekend, from Oct. 30 to Nov. 2, including the giant offering in the central Zócalo square, which will showcase a more than 30-meter-tall Catrina figure accompanied by 100,000 cempasúchil plants from the conservation area. A cempasúchil trail will also be set up in Chapultepec Park.

Visitors are also encouraged to go to Xochimilco to see performances of La Llorona or to join the Día de Muertos celebrations in the borough’s neighborhoods, where various cultural traditions will be on display over the weekend, including six theatrical performances at the piers, as well as activities in downtown Xochimilco.

With reports from El Economista and Excelsior

World.title: Brazil Draws US$11.3bn in Foreign Investment
World.content:
BRAZIL · ECONOMY

Published Wednesday, 28 October, 3:40 p.m. ET · Source: Banco Central do Brasil, external sector statistics note of 26 October 2026

Key Facts — Inflow Brazil received US$11.3 billion in net foreign direct investment in September 2026.

— Comparison That compares with US$9.6 billion in September 2025 and US$7.4 billion in August 2026.

— Twelve months Investment over the past year reached US$88.3 billion, or 3.43% of GDP.

— Contrast Foreign portfolio investment, in stocks and bonds, left Brazil with net outflows of US$2.1 billion.

What Happened

Brazil attracted US$11.3 billion in net foreign direct investment in September 2026, the Central Bank of Brazil reported on Monday, October 26, 2026. The inflow was up from US$9.6 billion in September 2025 and from US$7.4 billion in August 2026, according to the bank’s external sector note.

Equity participation made up US$8.1 billion of the total, split between US$4.3 billion in new capital and US$3.8 billion in reinvested earnings. Intercompany operations, which are loans and transfers between companies of the same group, added US$3.2 billion.

Over the 12 months through September, direct investment totaled US$88.3 billion, equal to 3.43% of gross domestic product. A month earlier the 12-month total stood at US$86.6 billion, or 3.39% of GDP.

Foreign portfolio investment moved the other way, with net outflows of US$2.1 billion in September. Brazil’s international reserves stood at US$362.8 billion at the end of the month.

Why It Matters

Direct investment is money that foreign companies commit to factories, stakes and operations in Brazil, and it tends to stay for years. Portfolio flows, by contrast, can leave within days when investors change their mind.

The September inflow arrived in the same release as Brazil’s balance with the rest of the world. Our report on the current account deficit covers that side of the release, and our August investment report covers the month before.

What It Means for You

For a US company or investor with exposure to Brazil, the figures show that long-term corporate money kept flowing in while financial investors pulled back from stocks and bonds. Direct investment is the steadier of the two signals, but one month does not make a trend.

About US$7 billion of the September total came from reinvested earnings and intercompany lending rather than fresh outside capital. That mix is common in the Central Bank’s accounts, yet it means the headline number is not all new money arriving from abroad.

What Is Not Known

The Central Bank’s note does not break the September inflow down by sector or by country of origin. It is therefore unclear which industries or which foreign investors drove the result.

It is also unclear how much of the intercompany lending is new financing and how much is a refinancing inside corporate groups. Monthly figures are often revised, and the note does not say whether this one will be.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is foreign direct investment in Brazil?

Foreign direct investment, known in Brazil as IDP, is money that foreign companies put into Brazilian operations through equity stakes, reinvested earnings and loans from parent companies. It differs from portfolio investment, which is the buying and selling of stocks and bonds.

How much did Brazil receive in September 2026?

Brazil received US$11.3 billion in net foreign direct investment, according to the Central Bank. The 12-month total reached US$88.3 billion, or 3.43% of GDP.

Why did portfolio investment fall while direct investment rose?

The two measure different kinds of money with different time horizons. In September, direct investment brought in US$11.3 billion while portfolio investment recorded net outflows of US$2.1 billion.

São Paulo woke up to blocked streets around its biggest concert ground, with BTS, the South Korean pop group, due on stage tonight. Our BTS in São Paulo page tracks every development.

The first of three sold-out shows starts at 7:00 p.m. Eastern Time. The road closures began the night before and are already testing the patience of local drivers.

What Happens Tonight and Over the Weekend

BTS plays the first of its three São Paulo shows tonight, Wednesday, 28 October, at 20:00 local time, which is 7:00 p.m. Eastern Time. Gates open at 16:00, and the other concerts follow on Friday, 30 October, and Saturday, 31 October, at the same hour.

The second CET phase is scheduled to start at 23:00 on Thursday, 29 October, and run until 01:30 on Sunday, 1 November. Delays are likely to peak when the gates open and when the crowd leaves after each show.

Organisers expect about 90,000 fans a night, and more than 250,000 across the three dates. That is a very large crowd for a stadium better known for football, and for streets built for a residential district.

The Ticket Dispute Still in the Background

Live Nation Brazil, the concert promoter, says the dates, sectors and ticket map are unchanged. Earlier this month a São Paulo consumer prosecutor, the public official who handles consumer-rights cases, asked the city, the ticket seller Ticketmaster Brasil and Live Nation to explain two conflicting seating plans.

The plans differ over standing areas called Pit 1 and Pit 2, which appeared in a plan in the city’s Official Gazette but not on the ticket map. Procon-SP, the São Paulo state consumer protection agency, separately notified the promoter and the ticket seller on 22 October about the stage, screens and tickets.

Other stops on the tour reportedly used 12 screens, against four central screens planned for South America. We found no report that either dispute has changed tonight’s schedule or invalidated tickets.

What It Means for Readers in the United States

Fans following from the United States should count in Eastern Time: São Paulo is one hour ahead until US clocks change on 1 November. That makes the 30 and 31 October shows start at 7:00 p.m. ET too.

Travellers with plans in the south-west of the city should allow extra time on show days, since the closures cover the main roads into Morumbi. The quickest way to check conditions is the traffic updates that CET publishes before each phase.

What Is Not Known

Final attendance and the length of the post-show delays are not yet known. It is also open whether Procon-SP or the prosecutor will take further steps before the weekend.

When does BTS play in São Paulo?

BTS plays MorumBIS stadium on 28, 30 and 31 October 2026. Each show starts at 20:00 São Paulo time, which is 7:00 p.m. Eastern Time.

Which roads are closed around MorumBIS?

CET closed parts of Avenida Giovanni Gronchi, Avenida Jorge João Saad and Avenida Jules Rimet, plus several squares and side streets. A second phase runs from 23:00 on 29 October to 01:30 on 1 November.

World.title: Miami Cubans Reject Deportations but Back Republicans
World.content:
A street sign in Little Havana, the heart of Miami’s Cuban community. File photo.

Published Wednesday, 28 October, 3:20 p.m. ET (3:20 p.m. Havana) · Source: Florida International University (FIU) Cuba Poll 2026, Polymarket

Miami’s Cuban Americans are angry about deportations, yet most of them still plan to vote Republican next week. A new survey by Florida International University (FIU), a university in Miami, found that 76% disapprove of the Trump administration’s push to deport more Cubans without criminal records. Even so, 68% say they will back the Republican for Congress on 3 November.

The result adds a twist to the wider story of cuba news and US politics. The community that fled Fidel Castro’s Cuba is split between its anger at Washington’s migration policy and its loyalty to the party that promises a hard line on Havana.

Key Facts What happened: 76% of Miami-Dade Cuban Americans oppose more Cuban deportations, but 68% would vote Republican for Congress.

76% of Miami-Dade Cuban Americans oppose more Cuban deportations, but 68% would vote Republican for Congress. The poll: FIU asked 1,004 Cuban American adults between 4 and 29 September; margin of error 3.1 points.

FIU asked 1,004 Cuban American adults between 4 and 29 September; margin of error 3.1 points. What happens next: Election Day is Tuesday, 3 November, with a Florida Senate seat and the governorship on the ballot.

Election Day is Tuesday, 3 November, with a Florida Senate seat and the governorship on the ballot. Why it matters for US readers: Florida’s Cuban vote shows whether a policy backlash can move a loyal bloc.

Florida’s Cuban vote shows whether a policy backlash can move a loyal bloc. Prediction markets: Polymarket gave Republican Ashley Moody 91.5% to win Florida’s Senate race (US$312,849 traded; 3:09 p.m. ET, 28 October).

This story is part of our coverage of the cuba news. Dates, times and how to follow it are in our guide. Latest: Cuba Embargo Vote Hits 1995 Low

In plain English Miami-Dade is the Florida county where most Cuban Americans live, and the FIU Cuba Poll has tracked their opinions since 1991. Pollsters asked people two separate questions, one about deportations and one about votes, and the answers point in opposite directions.

Anger That Does Not Change the Vote

The poll found that 76% disapprove of increased deportations of Cubans who have no criminal record. Opposition reaches into the president’s own party, because 63% of Republicans in the sample reject the policy too.

Yet the ballot choice barely moves. For the US House of Representatives, 68% back the Republican candidate in their district and 28% the Democrat, a gap of 40 points.

Among the registered voters in the sample, 53% call themselves Republicans, 27% independents and 18% Democrats.

What Cuban Americans Say They Want Instead

The wish list is concrete. 87% want Washington to resume processing immigration benefits for Cubans who already live in the United States, and 86% of Republicans agree.

The Senate and Governor Races

In the Senate race, Republican Ashley Moody, who was appointed to the seat in 2025, leads Democrat Angie Nixon 51% to 26% among respondents who named a choice. Many others had not yet decided.

For governor, Republican Byron Donalds, a US congressman, holds 60% against 24% for Democrat David Jolly. The share of undecided voters was large here too.

Shops on Calle Ocho in Little Havana. File photo. Photo: Sharon Hahn Darlin, CC BY 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons

What Prediction Markets Say

On Polymarket, a platform where users bet real money on events, traders put Moody’s chance of winning the Florida Senate seat at 91.5%. About US$312,849 has been traded on that market, as of 3:09 p.m. ET on 28 October.

Why we show this: prediction markets turn real-money bets into a live probability that moves within minutes of the news, which is why investors, campaigns and newsrooms in the United States now follow them closely. We show them next to polls and official results, never instead of them.

What It Means for US Readers

Florida’s Cuban voters have delivered Republican margins for years, and this poll suggests the bloc is holding even under strain. A backlash over deportations, if it comes, may show up later rather than in this election.

Watch the margins in Miami-Dade on 3 November for the first real test.

What Is Not Known

The poll covers Cuban Americans in Miami-Dade only, so it cannot speak for all Cubans in the United States.

A large share of voters was undecided in both statewide races, and how they will break is unknown. The poll also does not say which way the 63% of Republicans who oppose the deportations will vote.

Frequently Asked Questions

What did the 2026 FIU Cuba Poll find?

It found that 76% of Cuban Americans in Miami-Dade disapprove of increased deportations of Cubans without criminal records. It also found that 68% would vote for the Republican House candidate.

How reliable is the survey?

FIU surveyed 1,004 Cuban American adults in Miami-Dade, with a margin of error of plus or minus 3.1 points, meaning the true figure likely sits within that range. It covers Miami-Dade only.

EL SALVADOR · TRADE

Key Facts What is happening El Salvador’s goods trade deficit narrowed to US$1.13 billion in September 2026 from US$1.15 billion in August.

Versus forecast Analysts expected a deficit of US$1.2 billion, so the gap was about US$67 million smaller than forecast.

Why it matters El Salvador uses the US dollar, so it cannot weaken a currency to fix a trade gap.

What to watch Whether the gap keeps shrinking in October, and what the breakdown of exports and imports shows.

How big was El Salvador’s trade deficit in September 2026?

It is the value of a country’s exports minus its imports of goods over a period. A negative number means the country imported more than it exported.

World.title: Zimbabwe Inflation Rises to 4.3% in October

AFRICA · ZIMBABWE

Versus forecast Analysts had expected 4.0%, so prices rose 0.3 percentage points faster than the consensus forecast.

Prices Rise Faster Than Forecast

World.title: US Consumer Confidence Jumps to 91.7
World.content:
Rio Times Markets · United States

Key Facts Who. The Conference Board, a US business research group, publishes the index monthly.

What. Consumer confidence rose to 91.7 in October from 84.2 in September.

Versus forecast. Analysts expected 81, per the RT economic calendar, so the reading beat by 10.7 points.

Why it matters. Confident households tend to spend more, and spending drives most US growth.

What to watch. Whether the mood shows up in retail sales and hiring data.

American households turned noticeably more upbeat in October, with confidence far above what analysts had expected.

Confidence Rebounds in October

The Conference Board’s Consumer Confidence Index rose to 91.7 in October from 84.2 in September. The reading was released on Tuesday, 27 October 2026.

Analysts in the RT economic calendar had forecast 81. The result beat that by 10.7 points and added 7.5 points to the September level.

What Lifted the Mood

Both parts of the survey improved. The Present Situation Index, which tracks how households see current conditions, rose 8.6 points to 120.4.

The Expectations Index, which looks six months ahead, rose 6.9 points to 72.6. The Conference Board said the gain came mainly from better views of current and future business conditions.

Why It Matters Beyond the US

Consumer spending is the largest part of the US economy, so shifts in household mood are watched closely. Many Latin American exporters, from Mexican factories to Brazilian farms, sell into that demand.

A confident US shopper can mean steadier orders for those exporters. Their sales to the US depend on American demand holding up.

What Is Not Known Yet

Confidence is a survey of opinion, not a count of purchases. It is not yet clear whether the October mood will lead to higher spending in the shops.

The Conference Board’s own summary says confidence remains on a long-term downward trend, so one strong month does not yet make a turn. The November reading will show whether the rebound holds.

Sources: The Conference Board (Consumer Confidence Index, 27 October 2026); forecast and earlier values from the RT economic calendar. This is news, not investment advice.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the Consumer Confidence Index?

It is a monthly survey of US households run by The Conference Board. A higher number means households feel better about jobs, business conditions and income.

How big was the October jump?

The index rose 7.5 points to 91.7 from 84.2. Analysts had expected 81.

Why does it matter for markets?

Consumer spending is the largest part of the US economy. Investors watch confidence as an early hint of how much households will spend.

Does confidence always predict spending?

No. Households can feel gloomy and still spend, or the reverse. The index is one signal among many.

World.title: Fed Hold Matters for Brazil, Mexico, Africa
World.content:
MARKETS · FED

Published Wednesday, 28 October · Source: Federal Open Market Committee statement of 28 October 2026 (federalreserve.gov); RT economic calendar

Key Facts The decision The Fed kept its target range at 3.75% to 4% on 28 October, by 10 to 2.

The channel US rates set the cost of dollar debt for governments and companies abroad.

The exposure Remittances to Mexico, Central America and Africa are paid in dollars.

The gap We have no confirmed market moves for the real, peso or African currencies yet.

The Federal Reserve kept its key rate at 3.75% to 4% on Wednesday, and the effect reaches well beyond the United States. Latin American and African economies feel US rates through borrowing in dollars, through their currencies and through money sent home.

Two members of the Federal Open Market Committee voted for a quarter-point hike, so the decision was not unanimous. The statement said inflation remains elevated.

Dollar Debt And Borrowing Costs

Many governments and companies in Latin America and Africa have borrowed in US dollars. When US rates stay at a given level, the benchmark for the cost of that borrowing stays there too.

A hold keeps the starting point for new dollar loans and bond refinancing unchanged. It does not lower it.

Central Banks Watch The Fed

Central banks in Brazil, Mexico and Chile set their own rates, but they follow what the Fed does and says. A US rate that stays put gives them one less shock to manage.

Two dissents in favour of a hike show that the direction of US rates is still debated. That debate is one reason emerging-market policymakers stay careful.

Remittances And Dollar Income

Money sent home from the United States to Mexico, Central America and parts of Africa is paid in dollars. When the dollar and local currencies move against each other, the same transfer buys more or less at home.

The decision itself does not change those transfers. What matters is how the dollar behaves against local currencies in the coming days.

What It Means For Brazil

For Brazil, the immediate effect is a reduced risk of an additional near-term upward shock to U.S. interest rates. A higher U.S. rate typically makes dollar assets more attractive and can increase pressure on emerging-market currencies, financial conditions and capital flows.

Holding at 3.75%–4.00% avoids adding another increment to that pressure. The Brazilian implications remain conditional rather than settled.

If the Fed’s pause leads markets to expect a December hike, the dollar could still strengthen and Brazilian assets could face renewed volatility. If investors interpret the decision as the beginning of a longer pause, pressure on emerging-market financing conditions could ease.

Mexico And Africa

Mexico is particularly sensitive to U.S. monetary policy because of its close trade and financial links with the United States. A Fed hold may reduce immediate pressure on the peso and Mexican interest-rate markets compared with a surprise hike.

The effect depends on the Fed’s guidance and on whether markets continue to price a December increase. The same transmission channels matter across African economies: the cost of dollar borrowing, exchange-rate pressure, imported inflation and portfolio flows.

A pause avoids an immediate further tightening of global dollar liquidity, but rates remain restrictive and the prospect of a December hike continues to weigh on countries with substantial dollar-denominated debt or vulnerable currencies.

What Comes Next

The decision does not signal that the Fed has declared victory over inflation. The two dissenters wanted rates higher immediately, and market participants continued to anticipate the possibility of another increase at the December meeting.

What Is Not Known

We have no confirmed market reaction to the decision and no comments from the Fed news conference. The Committee next meets on 8 and 9 December, after the 3 November midterm elections, and we do not know what it will decide.

Exchange rates and bond yields in Latin America and Africa will show the effect over the coming days. This article will be updated once those moves are confirmed.

Frequently Asked Questions

Why do US interest rates matter for Latin America and Africa?

Many governments and companies there borrow in dollars, and US rates set the benchmark for that borrowing. They also influence currencies and the flow of investment into emerging markets.

Did the Fed change its rate on 28 October 2026?

No. The Federal Open Market Committee kept the target range at 3.75% to 4% by a 10 to 2 vote, with two members preferring a quarter-point hike.

Will remittances change after the decision?

The decision does not change remittances directly. What matters is how the dollar moves against local currencies, which we have not confirmed yet.

World.title: Fed Holds at 3.75% to 4%, Two Vote to Hike
World.content:
US ECONOMY · FED

Published Wednesday, 28 October · Source: Federal Open Market Committee statement of 28 October 2026 (federalreserve.gov); RT economic calendar

Key Facts The decision The Fed kept its federal funds target range at 3.75% to 4%.

The vote 10 to 2, with two members preferring a quarter-point rate hike.

The wording Inflation remains elevated, and economic activity is expanding at a strong pace.

The time Wednesday, 28 October 2026, at 2:00 p.m. Eastern (18:00 Lisbon).

The Federal Reserve left its key interest rate unchanged on Wednesday, but two of its decision-makers wanted to raise it. The Federal Open Market Committee, the group that sets US interest rates, kept the federal funds target range at 3.75% to 4% by a 10 to 2 vote.

The rate is the price banks charge each other for overnight loans, and it sets the baseline for borrowing costs across the dollar economy. Our economic calendar consensus expected the upper end of the range to stay at 4%.

Two Members Wanted A Hike

Lisa D. Cook and Beth M. Hammack voted against the decision. Both preferred to raise the target range by a quarter of a percentage point at this meeting.

Two votes for a hike show that part of the Committee sees prices as the bigger risk. The statement itself does not explain their reasoning.
