World.title: Spanish train crash leaves 68 dead, PM Sanchez declares 3 days of mourning
World.content:
Skip next section High-speed train crash in Spain: What do we know so far?

Rescue teams at work at the site of crash near Toledo Image: Violeta Santos Moura/REUTERS

At least 68 people have died after a high-speed publicly-run Renfe train collided into the back of a privately-run Iryo train that was stopped farther along the tracks on the line between Madrid and the southern city of Seville.

The trains crashed just after 9 a.m. on Wednesday, between the towns of Mora and Orgaz, near Toledo. About 540 people were on the two trains, local officials said.

More than 100 remain injured.

Spain's train accident is the deadliest in Europe since 2013

Wednesday's accident was the second train disaster to have taken place in Spain this year and the deadliest train crash in Europe since 2013.

The train crash earlier this year in Spain also took place on the same line, with the collision near Cordoba having killed 46 people in January.

Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez said in a televised address from near the accident site that "all of Spain" was in mourning.

He said the "terrible tragedy" would be investigated and vowed to address any failures that came to light.

Spain's Transportation Minister Oscar Puente said the crash resulted from an "inexplicable" decision by operators to have the high-speed train continue on its journey after a computer error had triggered a red signal closing down the stretch of track.

All major parties, apart from the far-right Vox party, cancelled their campaigning on Wednesday out of respect for the victims. Spaniards are set to head to the polls on November 29.

World.title: Is Iran headed to war or peace after Mecca alliance meeting?
World.content:
Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkey have taken their latest peace push directly to Tehran. Officially, it was to avert a new military escalation, but their diplomatic outreach can also be seen as a warning to Iran.

Amid rising fear that the US and Israel are preparing to launch new attacks on Iran after the US midterm election on November 3, three major Middle Eastern powers delivered a coordinated diplomatic message directly to Tehran.

Pakistan's army chief Asim Munir, Saudi Defense Minister Khalid bin Salman and Turkish intelligence chief Ibrahim Kalin all traveled to Iran to meet Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian and senior officials in Tehran this Monday. The three envoys serve as representatives for the Mecca defense pact — a military alliance of Islamabad, Riyad and Ankara, which was officially set up this summer.

Saudi Arabia said ⁠the ⁠trip aims to open negotiating channels and "prevent the return of military escalation." Details on the agenda, however, remain scarce.

Iran conflict: Could a new phase of the war be imminent? To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

A senior Pakistani official cited by the Reuters news agency said the talks focused on building a regional non-aggression network, in addition to US-Iran talks, Houthi rebels' attacks on Saudi Arabia, the Strait of Hormuz and the US naval blockade.

Another official said Pakistan's Munir presented Iran with a solution to the conflict that would offer something both to Washington and Iran, with the three Mecca states and Qatar acting as mediators. The source told Reuters US President Donald Trump previously gave Munir the go-ahead to try diplomacy.

Tehran presents the meeting as a success

Iran hailed the "very positive atmosphere" during the Tehran talks, even though no breakthroughs were officially announced.

"Very good discussions took place between us," Mohsen Rezaei, head of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, told state television. "I feel that a new atmosphere is emerging in the region."

Rezaei argued that regional security should be built by countries in West Asia themselves and without outside intervention.

A day later, Rezaei reportedly met Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei. Iranian state media said Khamenei called for protecting Iran's interests and maintaining Tehran's conditions for ending both the war and the current state of "neither war nor peace."

Meanwhile, Iran's President Masoud Pezeshkian travelled to Moscow for the Gas Exporting Countries Forum, where he met Russian President Vladimir Putin and Qatar's Emir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani, with Pezeshkian and the emir also discussing the war and the Strait of Hormuz.

These and other diplomatic contacts were framed by Tehran as evidence that the US is unable to diplomatically isolate the Iranian regime.

Are Turkey and Pakistan closing ranks with Saudi Arabia?

The united front presented by the three nations in Tehran, however, can also be seen as a show of force for the new Mecca defense alliance. It comes as the Saudis grow increasingly wary of the attacks on Saudi infrastructure launched by the Iran-allied Houthi militants.

Egypt ready to back Saudi Arabia's war against Houthis To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Under the terms of the Mecca agreement, an outside attack on one of the member states is to be regarded as an attack on all of them. The visit also came on the same day as Egypt's parliament agreeing to give military help to Ryad and take "all necessary measures" to help Saudi Arabia defend itself, in addition to the looming threat of the US and Israel.

"The presence of the three senior representatives at the same time sent the message that these countries are acting as a bloc," Babak Dorbeiki, a London-based political analyst and former official at Iran's Strategic Research Center, told DW.

Saudi Arabia has long been regarded as Iran's archrival in region. It has used its enormous wealth to counter Iran's influence, and now it can, at least in theory, also count on Pakistan's nuclear capability, and Turkey's conventional military strength.

At the same time, Dorbeiki argued that the Mecca pact is primarily designed for deterrence rather than offensive war. And having a defense pact does not mean its members want to fight Iran.

Dorbeiki believes the message from the bloc could therefore work in two directions: It can provide mediation, but continued escalation could also alter that position.

Ryad pushing for a 'diplomatic solution'

Saudi Arabia faces the most immediate dilemma. Further Houthi attacks have damaged its infrastructure and economy, but a wider war with Iran could threaten the investment and development projects at the heart of Riyadh's economic strategy.

"For Saudi Arabia, both the current situation and a war with Iran carry serious costs," Dorbeiki said. "Its preferred route is, therefore, a diplomatic solution."

What now for Saudi Arabia after Riyadh airport attack? To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Moreover, Pakistan has spent months mediating between Washington and Tehran, and has important relations with both. A direct conflict would also distract Islamabad from its long-standing security concerns involving India.

Turkey is a NATO member, but Dorbeiki said direct military support for Iran against the United States is highly improbable. The fact that Ankara sent intelligence chief Ibrahim Kalin rather than its foreign or defense minister also suggests a cautious approach.

Iran pursues diplomacy while preparing for fighting

Ali Asghar Shafieian, media advisor for Iran's President Masoud Pezeshkian, also rejected the perspective that the Mecca pact representatives were trying to present Tehran with an ultimatum.

He told DW that the three countries may also have wanted to demonstrate their own growing coordination, while showing that Iran remains part of regional diplomacy.

"You cannot conclude from this meeting alone that it was an ultimatum before an attack," Shafieian said.

He also noted that Iran, just like the US and Israel, could prepare for the possibility of further conflict while maintaining negotiations.

Mediator or enforcer? Pakistan's role in the Middle East To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

"Just as they use the opportunity to strengthen their military and defensive capabilities, Iran does the same," he said, adding that an agreement remains possible if Iran's political standing and what Tehran describes as its national dignity are respected.

Diplomatic game continues

Dorbeiki argued that Iran is following a familiar strategy of extending negotiations while avoiding real-world commitments.

The Houthi rebels are central to Tehran's calculation.

Tehran has not publicly offered the kind of guarantees over Houthi attacks that Riyadh would want. Dorbeiki believes Iran could seek to trade influence over such the attacks for concessions such as an end to US military pressure and broader steps toward ending the war.

The only apparent outcome of the Tehran meeting is to keep talking. For Iran, that might be enough of a signal that it is still a diplomatic partner rather than an enemy.

Edited by: Shamil Shams

World.title: El controlador de Atocha, al maquinista del AVE: “Desconecte y vuelva a conectar y reanude con marcha normal”
World.content:
Lugar del accidente de dos trenes de alta velocidad, uno de Renfe y otro de Iryo, que han colisionado a primera hora de este miércoles a la altura de la estación de Urda (Toledo).

El audio de esta noticia utiliza una voz sintética generada por Inteligencia Artificial y podría tener algunas inconsistencias.

Los audios de la tragedia muestran el error del responsable de Atocha. La maquinista del Iryo le avisó a cinco minutos de la tragedia de que estaba detenida y no podía arrancar el tren

Los tres audios clave de la tragedia, dos conexiones entre la maquinista del tren Iryo que estaba parado y el controlador de Atocha y uno del maquinista del AVE que venía por detrás y este mismo operador, demuestran con claridad los errores que se cometieron. El controlador da la orden al tren AVE, que estaba 25 kilómetros por detrás del Iryo, de que reinicie “la marcha normal”, y no a vista, como señalaba el protocolo, con una limitación de 40 kilómetros por hora. La maquinista del Iryo también recibe la misma orden, de reanudar “la marcha normal”, pero siete minutos después llama para decir que sigue detenida porque no puede reiniciar el tren y sin embargo nadie avisó al AVE ni siquiera ahí, a cinco minutos de la tragedia, de que tenía que frenar.

02:58 Conversación AVE - Adif Atocha

El audio clave entre el centro de control de Atocha y el AVE, que dura más de cinco minutos, es muy confuso en el arranque, donde se ve al controlador con muchas dudas, pero termina con una orden clara que según el Gobierno contraviene claramente el protocolo y está en el origen del accidente: reanudar la marcha normal cuando aún no ha comprobado que el tren que estaba delante se haya alejado lo suficiente -más de 30 kilómetros- para evitar una colisión.

Los dos hombres al final de la conversación redactan una especie de acta de las órdenes que está recibiendo el maquinista, para que quede claro que ambos entienden lo mismo:

-CRC Atocha a maquinista de tren es 2080

-Sí

-A las 08.36.

-Sí

Y esto dice: maquinista de tren 2080. Desconecte y vuelva a conectar y vuelva a conectar el LZB. Reanude marcha. Y luego reanude la marcha al amparo del BSL con marcha normal

-Con marcha normal?

-Sí.

00:53 Conversación Iryo - Adif Atocha (1)

Ahí está el primer gran error, según el Ejecutivo, ordenar al AVE que reanude la marcha a las 8.36, cuando aún no ha comprobado que el iryo se está alejando, y además hacerlo a marcha normal, sin el protocolo de seguridad de marcha “a vista”, que podría haber evitado el accidente.

02:11 Conversación Iryo - Adif Atocha (2)

Los otros dos audios también apuntan claramente a otros dos errores, puesto que la maquinista avisó de que seguía detenida al no haber podido reanudar la marcha pese a haber recibido la autorización para ello.

8. 41: Primera llamada con el Iryo.

-Buenos días, Atocha. He tenido una pérdida de transmisión circulando en BZL. El siguiente se ha de ir en el 113 a más de 200. Pero no he cogido transmisión. Estoy detenida. A la entrada de La señal de entrada de Urda.

Después de varios mensajes confusos, el controlador finalmente sigue el protocolo y se dispone a dar las órdenes y firmar esa especie de acta conjunta para que quede claro que ambos han entendido lo mismo:

-Vale, pues un momentito. Esto dice maquinista de tren 6076. Desconecte. Y vuelva a conectar.

-Y vuelva a conectar.

-Reanude la marcha, al amparo del BFL, con marcha normal.

De nuevo, el controlador vuelve a dar la orden, también al Iryo, pero cuatro minutos después que al AVE, a pesar de que está delante y muy cerca, de que reanude con marcha normal.

Pero hay un tercer mensaje también desconcertante, tal vez el más evidente porque ahí aún se podía haber evitado la tragedia: el Iryo llama para decir que no puede arrancar, y aparentemente el controlador no toma ninguna decisión drástica con esa información ni avisa al AVE de que se detenga, cuando aún estaba a tiempo.

Audio 2 con el Iryio. 8.48.

Maquinista: No me está permitiendo el tren revisar el sistema el LZB. Y por eso estoy todavía detenida ante la señal de entrada.

Control: Vale. ¿Conforme? Pues nada, en cuanto pueda. Y si tiene problema, ahora nos llama.

Maquinista: Vale, perfecto. Ahora le digo.

Y ahí empieza una conversación interna que muestra un cierto caos en el centro de control: De verdad, tronco. De verdad. El 6071 está teniendo problemas con el equipo. Está avanzando hasta que se detenga. Tenía un meta 40 que continuara en BSL. No hemos cambiado. Un momento.

Cinco minutos después de esta conversación, se produjo el choque mortal del AVE con el Iryo sin que aparentemente nadie fuera consciente de que estaba a punto de llegar.

World.title: Última hora del accidente de trenes en Toledo, en directo | Al menos 68 muertos en el choque de trenes de alta velocidad en Urda
World.content:
Servicios de emergencia trabajan en el lugar del accidente de dos trenes de alta velocidad, uno de Renfe y otro de Iryo, que han colisionado a primera hora de este miércoles a la altura de la estación de Urda (Toledo)

107 hospitalizados en Castilla-La Mancha, 18 en estado crítico| Sánchez: “No es asumible dos accidentes de alta velocidad en menos de un año” | Feijóo: “España tiene derecho a saber el estado de sus infraestructuras”

Al menos 68 personas han muerto en un accidente ferroviario que se ha producido este miércoles por la mañana a la altura de la estación de Urda (Toledo). Solo en los hospitales de Castilla-La Mancha hay 107 personas ingresadas, según el servicio de emergencias 112 de la región, y 18 de los heridos están en estado crítico. Desde el lugar del accidente, el presidente del Gobierno, Pedro Sánchez, ha dicho que la investigación “llegará hasta el final y, si ha habido negligencias, se sabrá”, y ha afirmado que “no es asumible para un país como España” sufrir dos accidentes graves en la alta velocidad en menos de un año. El ministro de Transportes, Óscar Puente, ha calificado de “absolutamente inverosímil” e “inexplicable” el accidente. El líder del PP, Alberto Núñez Feijóo, ha asegurado que “España tiene derecho a saber qué está pasando con sus infraestructuras”.

Renfe ha puesto a disposición el número 900 10 10 20. Iryo, por su parte, ha habilitado el 900 001 403. El Servicio de Emergencias 112 de Castilla-La Mancha activado el 900 122 112.

World.title: Puente califica de “inexplicable” que el centro de control permitiera al AVE reanudar la marcha con normalidad cuando el Iryo seguía parado
World.content:
El ministro de Transportes, Óscar Puente, ha calificado de “inexplicable” que el centro de control de Adif autorizara al tren de alta velocidad de Renfe a reanudar la marcha con normalidad cuando el convoy de Iryo seguía detenido en la vía. Aunque todavía no está claro por qué se dio esa orden ni cómo pudo producirse el choque en esas circunstancias, la versión oficial apunta a que al menos un maquinista de otro tren advirtió al centro de control de que, tras el fallo del sistema de seguridad y de comunicación que se produjo en torno a las 8:30 horas, no se podía circular con normalidad y era necesario avanzar a marcha vista, es decir, con el maquinista avanzando a una velocidad máxima de 40 kilómetros por hora y preparado para detenerse ante cualquier obstáculo.

Puente ha explicado que se enteró del accidente pocos minutos antes de las nueve de la mañana y que se trasladó de inmediato al centro de control de Adif en Atocha para conocer los detalles del siniestro. Llegó sobre las 9:40 horas y, desde entonces, se ha reunido con los técnicos del centro que disponían de información sobre lo ocurrido para tratar de esclarecer las causas del choque. El accidente ferroviario, ocurrido entre Los Yébenes y Urda (Toledo), en la línea de alta velocidad entre Madrid y Andalucía, se ha saldado con al menos 68 víctimas mortales y más de 50 heridos, según los datos facilitados por las autoridades. La colisión provocó el descarrilamiento de varios vagones, algunos de los cuales cayeron por un terraplén. Más de 540 personas viajaban en los dos trenes siniestrados, según los datos confirmados por las autoridades.

Según la reconstrucción de los hechos ofrecida por el ministro en la comparecencia, sobre las 8:30 horas se produjo un fallo de comunicación en tres ordenadores de la red que dejó fuera de servicio el sistema de control y seguridad LZB en un tramo de 63 kilómetros a la altura de la estación de Urda (Toledo). La incidencia provocó la detención automática de todos los trenes que circulaban por ese tramo, seis según una estimación provisional que Puente ha advertido que todavía debe comprobarse. Con los convoyes detenidos y sin el sistema LZB operativo, el centro de control de Adif en Atocha asumió la gestión del tráfico ferroviario de forma manual.

A las 8:36 horas, el centro de control autorizó al tren de Renfe que acabó colisionando con el Iryo a reanudar la marcha “con normalidad” pese a que, según Puente, debía permanecer detenido. El ministro ha explicado que el convoy tenía una indicación de parada obligatoria y que tanto la normativa como los protocolos de Adif impedían que retomara la circulación en esas condiciones. Además, el circuito de vía seguía ocupado por el tren de Iryo, detenido a la entrada de la estación, y una señal roja que prohibía reanudar la marcha. Pese a ello, el tren de Renfe recorrió unos 25 kilómetros durante los aproximadamente 17 minutos transcurridos hasta el impacto, que se produjo a las 8:53 horas. La velocidad que alcanzó todavía se desconoce, aunque en ese tramo puede llegar hasta los 200 kilómetros por hora, según ha detallado el ministro.

La reconstrucción de Puente apunta a que el accidente se produjo después de que el centro de control autorizara al tren de Renfe a reanudar la marcha con normalidad, pese a que compartía el mismo cantón —el tramo de vía en el que no puede haber dos trenes en esas condiciones— con el Iryo, que seguía detenido. Según ha explicado el ministro, el maquinista de otro tren que no estuvo involucrado en el choque advirtió al centro de control que, tras el fallo del sistema de seguridad, la circulación no podía reanudarse con normalidad, sino que debía hacerse a marcha vista. El operario reconoció que el maquinista tenía razón y corrigió la instrucción para ese convoy. Sin embargo, al tren de Renfe que acabaría chocando con el Iryo se le había ordenado reanudar la marcha con normalidad, de ahí que terminara colisionando.

Puente ha señalado que hubo tiempo para corregir esa decisión, que ha calificado de “errónea”, antes de que se produjera el impacto. El ministro ha añadido que cree que el Iryo recibió también alguna instrucción para reanudar la marcha, pero que desconoce por qué no lo hizo y que todavía no dispone de información concluyente sobre ese punto. A pesar de esto, ha insistido en que serán las investigaciones futuras las que determinen quiénes son los responsables. “Yo les doy los hechos, que son así, irrefutables”, ha afirmado, y ha asegurado que comparecerá de nuevo las veces que sea necesario para aclarar las incógnitas que siguen pendientes.

Preguntado por si se plantea dimitir tras el accidente, ha rechazado centrar la atención en su futuro político y ha insistido en que ahora la prioridad es esclarecer lo ocurrido y atender las consecuencias del siniestro. “No es momento de pensar en mí, sino en las víctimas y sus familias”. “Estamos absolutamente devastados. Toda mi solidaridad y empatía con ellos”, ha señalado.

World.title: Feijóo, sobre el accidente ferroviario: “España tiene derecho a saber qué está pasando con sus infraestructuras”
World.content:
El líder del Partido Popular, Alberto Núñez Feijóo, ha reclamado explicaciones sobre el accidente ferroviario de Toledo, que ha provocado al menos 68 muertos y 77 heridos, así como una investigación gubernamental y judicial “inmediata” y “sin interferencias”. Feijóo, que ha comparecido de urgencia en la sede del PP en una declaración sin preguntas y con un crespón negro a su espalda, ha instado además a una “revisión completa e independiente de toda la red ferroviaria”. “España tiene derecho a saber qué está pasando con sus infraestructuras, en qué estado se encuentran las vías y los sistemas de seguridad y qué advertencias se recibieron desde Adamuz y qué medidas se adoptaron”, ha pedido el jefe de la oposición.

Feijóo ha expresado un primer mensaje de acompañamiento en el dolor a las familias de las víctimas y de reconocimiento al trabajo de los servicios de emergencia, sanitarios y vecinos que se están volcando en atender a los afectados. “No hay angustia comparable a esa espera. La sentimos en carne propia porque también la hemos sufrido y sufrimos con gente muy querida para nosotros. Saben que me refiero a la exministra Fátima Báñez, de quien todavía no tenemos noticias confirmadas”, ha afirmado el líder del PP sobre la dirigente popular, exministra de Trabajo de 59 años que viajaba en uno de los trenes siniestrados y que todavía se encuentra desaparecida.

“Este es el momento del respeto a los muertos, a los heridos y a sus familiares”, ha defendido el líder del PP, pero “serenidad no es silencio”, ha afirmado Feijóo, y ha pedido explicaciones. “Los españoles se hacen preguntas con exigencia y merecen respuestas”, ha instado el jefe de los populares, que no ha reclamado responsabilidades políticas porque considera que todavía “no es el día” por el respeto a los fallecidos. “Es imprescindible una investigación gubernamental inmediata y otra judicial, en los tiempos que procedan, con todos los medios y sin interferencias”, ha reclamado Feijóo. “España tiene derecho a saber qué está pasando con sus infraestructuras, en qué estado se encuentran las vías y los sistemas de seguridad, y qué advertencias se recibieron desde Adamuz y qué medidas se adoptaron. Los españoles tienen derecho a una revisión completa e independiente de toda la red ferroviaria. Ya es inaplazable. Y los españoles tienen derecho a que se rinda cuentas de cada euro. Lo que se anunció y lo que de verdad se ejecutó, lo que se recibió y en qué se gastó. Garantizo que todo esto lo tendrá”.

El accidente ocurrido pocos minutos antes de las 9.00, cuando un tren de Renfe ha chocado contra uno de Iryo que se encontraba parado en la vía a la altura de la estación de Urda (Toledo), ha provocado ya 68 muertos. Las primeras hipótesis, según ha afirmado esta mañana el ministro de Transportes, Óscar Puente, señalan que se trata de un error humano derivado de que uno de los operarios del Centro de Control de Atocha ha dado la orden de retomar la marcha con normalidad al conductor de Renfe cuando el de Iryo se estaba estacionado a tan solo 25 kilómetros de distancia.

“Una nación herida debe obtener la confianza de que este país puede volver a funcionar”, ha concluido el líder del PP, que participará hoy a las ocho de la tarde en un minuto de silencio por las víctimas frente al Ayuntamiento de Madrid.

World.title: Las grúas llegan al lugar del accidente tren de Urda para comenzar las labores de rescate: “La prioridad es localizar a las vícitmas atrapadas”
World.content:
Las grúas llegan al lugar del accidente tren de Urda para comenzar las labores de rescate: “La prioridad es localizar a las vícitmas atrapadas”

World.title: La victoria de los partidos árabes de Israel: récord de escaños frente al racismo y la discriminación
World.content:
Si el bloque anti-Netanyahu desea formar un Gobierno, está obligado a negociar con estas formaciones. El partido del primer ministro denuncia que “robaron las elecciones”

Un día después de las elecciones legislativas no está nada claro quién será el próximo primer ministro de Israel, pero lo que nadie discute es que entre los vencedores claros de las votaciones están los partidos árabes, que lograron una movilización ciudadana histórica y ponen al bloque judío anti-Netanyahu ante un dilema muy complicado: echar al actual Gobierno o seguir despreciando el voto de esta parte de la sociedad.

“Cualquiera que quiera ofrecer una alternativa al Ejecutivo sangriento de Netanyahu tendrá que hablar con nosotros para allanar el camino hacia el cambio que anhela la ciudadanía israelí”, ha apuntado Yousef Jabareen, líder de la Lista Conjunta, coalición de tres partidos que ha logrado 12 escaños a falta de conocer el escrutinio final. La otra formación arabe que participó en las elecciones, la islamista moderada Ra’am, obtuvo otros siete, también a falta de conocer los resultados definitivos.

Uniendo todos los votos, el bloque anti-Netanyahu supera sin problemas los 61 escaños necesarios para tener mayoría en un Parlamento de 120 diputados. Pero la realidad es más complicada y pone de manifiesto las grietas de la democracia israelí y el racismo que la impregna, que hace que no todos los ciudadanos del país sean iguales. Tampoco sus votos lo son.

“Parece que los ciudadanos palestinos de Israel acudieron a votar para salvar al Estado de Israel de sí mismo. La pregunta ahora es: ¿Quiere Israel ser salvado?“, lanza Yehuda Shaul, codirector del centro de reflexión Ofek. “Tendremos que esperar y ver si los que se oponen a Netanyahu quieren salvar a Israel del fascismo o prefieren seguir demonizando a los palestinos ciudadanos de Israel”.

En la legislatura que termina, estos partidos árabes tuvieron un total de 10 diputados. Ahora, si no se cuenta con ellos para gobernar, Israel puede verse abocado a volver a las urnas en medio año. Y hasta entonces, Netanyahu seguiría siendo primer ministro.

El líder del partido Ra'am, Mansour Abbas, el martes en Maghar (Israel). Rami Shlush (REUTERS)

Tres de los cuatro partidos judíos contrarios al primer ministro se han opuesto o mostrado reacios en campaña a negociar con las dos formaciones árabes, que representan, esencialmente, a los palestinos con nacionalidad israelí, la quinta parte de la población del país.

“Fue decepcionante, aunque no sorprendente, ver cómo minutos después de conocer los sondeos a pie de urna, el líder del llamado bloque del ‘cambio’ apeló a formar un Gobierno de mayoría sionista y cayó en la trampa que Netanyahu le tendió durante la campaña”, escribe este miércoles Noa Landau, directora adjunta del diario israelí Haaretz, refiriéndose a Gadi Eisenkot.

El líder opositor ha asegurado en varias ocasiones que los partidos árabes no cumplen las condiciones para poder negociar con ellos. Entre ellas, reconocer a Israel como un Estado judío y democrático o calificar a la milicia islamista Hamás de organización terrorista. Naftalí Bennett y Avigdor Lieberman rechazan pactar con ellos, pero también lo hacían antes de firmar el acuerdo de coalición con uno de ellos, Ra’am, en 2021, lo que significó la entrada de un partido árabe en un Gobierno israelí. El Ejecutivo duró poco, pero fue algo histórico.

La coalición de izquierda Los Demócratas, que también forma parte del bloque anti-Netanyahu y que agrupa al laborismo y al partido pacifista Meretz, se desmarca de esta postura. “No tenemos futuro si no dejamos de tener miedo. No podemos aceptar más la división racista de Netanyahu entre votos judíos y votos árabes”, ha dicho este miércoles su líder, Yair Golán, que considera que la voz de un ciudadano israelí que vota en la ciudad árabe de Tayibe es exactamente igual que la voz de un ciudadano israelí que vota en Givat Shmuel, una ciudad mayoritariamente judía. “Quien intenta borrar las voces de los ciudadanos árabes, se rinde ante Netanyahu y renuncia a Israel”, ha recalcado.

Desde el cierre de las urnas el martes, el líder de Ra’am, Mansur Abbas, manifestó su voluntad de unirse a una mayoría contra Netanyahu, como hizo en 2021-2022.

”Nuestro público quiere que influyamos en el sistema político. La Lista Conjunta quiere ayudar y allanar el camino para un gobierno alternativo. Y por eso estamos extendiendo la mano al Bloque del Cambio", dijo por su parte este miércoles Ahmad Tibi, número dos de la Lista Conjunta, dando a entender que había negociaciones en marcha.

En estos días, este experimentado diputado ya dio a entender que la Lista Conjunta podría votar con la oposición a Netanyahu en algunas cosas, abstenerse en otras. Es decir, ser una especie de aliado al margen, que no obstaculice el quehacer del Gobierno, pero que tampoco forme parte plenamente de él.

Pero Netanyahu parece dispuesto a impedir estos pactos. Este miércoles, su partido, el Likud, publicó un comunicado en el que afirma que las elecciones “fueron robadas por partidos árabes que apoyan al terrorismo y la destrucción del Estado judío”.

La formación explicó que ha presentado “cientos de testimonios y pruebas” a la policía y las autoridades electorales relacionadas con este presunto “fraude cometido en numerosos colegios electorales árabes”. El Likud cita, por ejemplo, “miles de sobres con dinero en efectivo junto a las papeletas del partido Ra’am, amenazas y actos de violencia dirigidos contra el personal de los colegios electorales”, o personas que votaron con identidad falsa.

Más discriminados desde 2023

El sentimiento de los palestinos con nacionalidad israelí, descendientes de los que permanecieron dentro de las fronteras trazadas tras la creación del Estado en 1948, sin embargo, es que sus voces nunca han sido iguales ni el Estado les ha protegido. Tras los ataques de Hamás en Israel, el 7 de octubre de 2023, la discriminación y los ataques racistas y contra su libertad de expresión han aumentado peligrosamente.

En septiembre, el Comité Electoral Central de Israel vetó la participación de las dos listas árabes en los comicios, argumentando que rechazaban la existencia de Israel como Estado judío y democrático y que apoyaban la lucha armada. La decisión fue posteriormente revocada por el Tribunal Supremo, que sí mantuvo la inhabilitación de Sami Abu Shehada, presidente del partido Balad.

Cuatro días antes de las elecciones, Tibi manifestaba a este diario que la manera de dar la vuelta a esta situación era ir a votar. Este experimentado político, que lleva más de 20 años siendo diputado, estimaba que si un 70% del electorado árabe acudía a las urnas, el escenario político cambiaría. Finalmente, la participación de esta minoría podría haber rozado el 80%. En noviembre de 2022, en las últimas elecciones legislativas, la participación en las localidades árabes fue del 53,2%.

“Tenemos mayoría. Tenemos responsabilidad. Y tenemos la oportunidad de formar un Gobierno de cambio en unión con los ciudadanos árabes de Israel”, ha insistido Golán, de Los Demócratas.

“Haremos que nuestras demandas se escuchen, comenzando por más seguridad para nuestra comunidad”, ha aseverado Tibi. La lucha contra el crimen organizado es una de las grandes preocupaciones de los palestinos de Israel. En 2025, se registraron 241 homicidios entre las comunidades árabes de Israel, frente a los 47 registrados entre la población judía, según cifras oficiales.

World.title: La UE y Canadá buscan una alianza histórica tras descartar la fórmula de “miembro asociado”
World.content:
Los líderes de la UE, Ursula von der Leyen y António Costa reciben al primer ministro de Canadá, Mark Carney, en la sede del Consejo de la UE en Bruselas, en 2025.

Son muchas las dudas y grandes las expectativas para la Cumbre UE-Canadá que se celebra este jueves y viernes en Montreal, y en la que se espera que se sienten las bases de una nueva alianza entre ambas potencias. Y aunque el estatus de “miembro asociado” que la presidenta de la Comisión Europea, Ursula von der Leyen, planteó para Canadá ha quedado finalmente fuera del borrador final, la ambición compartida para la cumbre es lograr acuerdos de carácter histórico que reconfiguren el tablero de influencias.

El primer ministro canadiense, Mark Carney, que prefiere enmarcar la nueva relación en lo que ambas partes llaman “alianza para el futuro”, dejó claro el domingo en un comunicado que el contexto determina la urgencia: “El mundo se ha vuelto más peligroso y más polarizado”, decía la nota. Una preocupación que también se destila en la agenda de la cumbre, publicada el martes y que prioriza la geopolítica.

Más información Von der Leyen apuesta por que Canadá sea el primer miembro asociado de la UE

Maria Popova, politóloga de la Universidad McGill, sostiene: “Se trata de países afines que se sienten cada vez más presionados y aislados en un mundo geopolítico en el que los adversarios se están volviendo más agresivos y el gran aliado, Estados Unidos, es cada vez menos fiable. Ese es realmente el motor de esta relación. Lo demás es, por así decirlo, cómo dar un esqueleto concreto a este alineamiento geopolítico, pero no es realmente lo que lo impulsa”.

Encabezan la agenda de la cumbre el compromiso con el multilateralismo y el orden internacional basado en normas, y la cooperación para promover la paz y la seguridad internacionales, con un claro adversario: Rusia. Popova explica que además de que “Europa y Canadá ven a Rusia como un actor realmente agresivo y problemático en estos momentos”, un acercamiento ruso-estadounidense “sería sin duda el peor escenario posible tanto para Canadá como para Europa”.

Mark Carney y Ursula von der Leyen en el Parlamento Europeo en septiembre. Yves Herman (REUTERS)

Se prevé también que haya un compromiso común para aumentar el apoyo a Ucrania. Popova señala que, en materia de defensa, Canadá puede aportar inversión y cooperación: “Es un momento muy importante en el que Ucrania está liderando la innovación en tecnología de drones, pero hacen falta inversión, producción y cadenas de suministro en otros lugares para convertir esto en un sistema realmente eficaz, en el que tanto Europa como Canadá puedan salir reforzadas juntas y reducir su dependencia común de Estados Unidos en este terreno”.

El esqueleto concreto al alineamiento geopolítico del que habla Popova vendrá de la mano de acuerdos de cooperación sectorial, que se sumarán al Acuerdo Económico y Comercial Global (CETA, por sus siglas en inglés), el tratado de libre comercio entre Canadá y la UE, que precisamente cumple 10 años este viernes

El canadiense Mark Camilleri, CEO de la Asociación de Comercio e Inversión Canadá-UE, con sede en Bruselas, destaca el nuevo acuerdo de comercio digital, que se negocia desde marzo y que muchos, como él, cuentan con que se materialice para el fin de semana. “Lleva el CETA al terreno de la infraestructura digital, y va a ayudar a aliviar algunas de las cargas que tienen las empresas cuando comercian en el extranjero, por ejemplo, en cuanto a la facilitación de la facturación y el almacenamiento de datos. Tiene más que ver con la arquitectura, pero aun así es muy interesante y las empresas lo están siguiendo”, dice Camilleri, que desde hace 20 años se dedica a impulsar la inversión y las relaciones comerciales a través del Atlántico.

Otro anuncio importante relativo al comercio es la conexión de los sistemas de pago instantáneo de ambos lados del Atlántico, que permitiría transacciones transfronterizas más rápidas y baratas y, según los analistas, reduciría la dependencia de redes estadounidenses como Visa o Mastercard. La medida cobra especial relevancia tras las sanciones que la Administración de Donald Trump impuso en 2025 a figuras como la jueza canadiense del Tribunal Penal Internacional Kimberly Prost o la relatora especial de la ONU para los territorios palestinos ocupados, Francesca Albanese. Ambas se quedaron temporalmente sin poder usar sus tarjetas de crédito y perdieron el acceso a servicios de empresas estadounidenses.

Para Camilleri, la clave de todos estos acuerdos está en un concepto que Carney repite desde hace meses: la soberanía. “¿Qué necesita un país para que se le considere soberano, para que no se le pueda obligar a hacer cosas contrarias a sus intereses por parte de terceros países u otros actores?”, plantea. A la idea tradicional de “defender a tu país, alimentar a tu país”, explica, el primer ministro canadiense ha sumado otros ámbitos, como los sistemas de pago o las vacunas.

La otra palabra clave es complementariedad: “Canadá y la UE no aportan lo mismo”. Canadá ofrece “recursos naturales, energía, materias primas, de cuya importación Europa depende en gran medida”, desde el gas natural licuado hasta el hidrógeno o la energía nuclear, además de mano de obra cualificada. Europa, que “sigue siendo una superpotencia de la fabricación avanzada”, aporta un mercado enorme, capacidad para escalar tecnologías como la inteligencia artificial y, sobre todo, capital, porque explotar los recursos canadienses “requiere una cantidad de capital considerable que Canadá no puede aportar por sí sola”.

En este sentido, un borrador de la declaración conjunta que se publicará al término de la cumbre, recoge un acuerdo para facilitar la inversión del Banco Europeo de Inversiones en recursos críticos canadienses, “en particular, minerales críticos”, y su exportación a Europa. Según explicó a la agencia The Canadian Press Wendy Gilmour, vicepresidenta del instituto de estudios de defensa Conference of Defence Associations Institute, la medida busca reducir la dependencia del mercado estadounidense y de las cadenas de suministro chinas. “Dependemos demasiado del procesamiento en el extranjero”, señaló.

Mark Carney saluda a la jefa de la Asamblea de las Primeras Naciones, Cindy Woodhouse Nepinak, el 26 de octubre en Ottawa. Justin Tang (Justin Tang/The Canadian Press v)

Los borradores filtrados apuntan a otros anuncios: acceso de empresas canadienses a contratos europeos de nube e inteligencia artificial, el estudio de nuevos cables submarinos entre Europa, Canadá y Asia, negociaciones para que Canadá participe en el sistema de navegación por satélite Galileo y en el programa Erasmus, y más cooperación en defensa, del Ártico al mar Negro.

El embajador de Canadá ante la UE, Jonathan Wilkinson, aclaraba también esta semana en una entrevista con The Canadian Press que las negociaciones no contemplan la libre circulación de trabajadores, pero sí facilitar el acceso a mano de obra en algunos sectores especializados. “No hablamos de libre circulación de trabajadores entre Europa y Canadá. Pero en algunos ámbitos especializados puede ser interesante y útil para ambos poder recurrir a [sus respectivas] reservas de mano de obra”, explicó.

En definitiva, la cumbre de Montreal dará el pistoletazo de salida a un marco de cooperación de gran alcance, cuyo hilo conductor es la soberanía. Si Canadá acabará siendo miembro asociado de la UE o si la nueva relación se quedará en la llamada “alianza para el futuro” es algo que, para muchos, es lo de menos. “Las palabras exactas ni siquiera son lo más importante. Lo que más nos importa es ver qué significa eso en concreto”, dice Popova. Camilleri coincide: “Si acabamos con lo de miembro asociado o con otra cosa, da igual. Lo principal es que tenemos esta ambición”. La ambición de dos socios que, ante todo, defienden su independencia ante la agresividad creciente de Rusia, la dependencia de China y la imprevisibilidad de la Administración de Donald Trump.

World.title: Un colaborador de Leire Díez califica de “bulo” el supuesto intento de agresión a la jueza Beatriz Biedma
World.content:
El exmagistrado Luis Sáenz de Tejada, señalado como colaborador de la trama del caso Leire Díez, ha calificado este miércoles de “bulo” el supuesto encargo para agredir físicamente a la jueza Beatriz Biedma, que dirigió la investigación contra el hermano de Pedro Sánchez. Citado como imputado en la Audiencia Nacional, Sáenz de Tejada se ha desvinculado ante el juez instructor Santiago Pedraz de toda conspiración para atentar contra Biedma o acosarla; y ha limitado sus contactos con Leire Díez a un intento de difundir la red de corrupción que, según él, se extiende en los tribunales de Badajoz, donde fue condenado por violencia machista —lo que implicó su expulsión de la carrera en 2019—.

El sumario del caso Leire Díez se centra en cómo Leire Díez y Santos Cerdán, ex secretario de Organización del PSOE, trataron presuntamente de boicotear pesquisas judiciales que salpicaban al partido y al Gobierno. Biedma, que se ha personado como víctima en la Audiencia Nacional, relató ante Pedraz que se sintió amenazada en aquella época tras sospechar que había sufrido seguimientos, y añadió que le contaron que Sáenz de Tejada había contactado con Cintia Rocho, alias Celsa, una mujer vinculada a un presunto clan de narcos. Rocho aseguró a la Guardia Civil que el exjuez le dijo que la magistrada de Badajoz “era un puto grano en el culo y que había que eliminarla”. Una acusación que él niega: “Nunca hablé con Cintia”.

Esa es la versión que Sáenz de Tejada ha repetido este miércoles: “Todo esto no deja de ser un montaje para acabar con las denuncias de corrupción en Badajoz y, de paso, en una campaña electoral, intentar vincularlo con el PSOE”, ha dicho. “Jamás he tenido contacto [con Rocho], jamás me he dirigido a ella”, ha reiterado. El exmagistrado ha incidido, además, en que nunca recibió ningún encargo ni pagos de Leire Díez y que sus contactos se enmarcan dentro de su actividad como denunciante de casos de corrupción, según explican fuentes jurídicas presentes en la declaración.

El exjuez —imputado por cuatro delitos (contra la integridad moral, organización criminal, calumnias y coacciones)— ha subrayado que se vio con Leire Díez, al igual que desde 2013 se ha reunido con muchos “políticos y periodistas”, para denunciar la corrupción de los juzgados de Badajoz. Su objetivo, según ha dicho, era dar difusión a la trama de la ciudad pacense que le costó la carrera, y le contaron que la entonces militante socialista tenía contactos en el PSOE y era reportera. Sáenz de Tejada ha añadido al respecto que Leire Díez no es más que una “anécdota” en su vida de “lucha contra la corrupción”.

Paralelamente, Pedraz ha tomado este miércoles declaración como testigo a la subdirectora adjunta de Nacionalidad y Estado Civil, dependiente del Ministerio de Justicia. La fiscal le ha preguntado por la obtención de la nacionalidad española por parte de Nervis Villalobos, un exviceministro venezolano que presuntamente recurrió a la trama. La subdirectora ha subrayado que no apreciaron ninguna irregularidad en esa tramitación.

World.title: Jetten calls for tougher sanctions against Russia ahead of talks
World.content:
Prime minister Rob Jetten has called for Europe to present a united front and step up sanctions against Russia in order to force Vladimir Putin to negotiate an end to the war in Ukraine.

Jetten told reporters at a joint president with Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelenskyy in The Hague that economic pressure was needed to persuade Putin to give ground.

His remarks came after Polish president Donald Tusk said the US, Ukraine and Russia had provisionally agreed to hold ceasefire talks in Abu Dhabi on November 4.

European leaders will not be present, but Tusk said Finnish president Alexander Stubb and Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre had held a call with Putin after consulting Zelenskyy and the American side.

Zelenskyy told reporters in The Hague that it was “very important” for Europe to show unity “because Russia is focusing on how to divide us”.

“Russia is losing,” he said. “The American side is asking to find a balance and a compromise. If they need a compromise, we say: Russia is not winning. But what is very clear is they are not ending the war.

No Russian gas

“That is the problem. That’s why we need to work step by step and move Russia to end this war.”

Jetten also ruled out restarting supplies of Russian gas to Europe, an idea reportedly raised by Donald Trump’s peace envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff during talks with Zelenskyy at the weekend.

“It is clear that we need to push Putin to take the negotiations seriously,” he said.

“The way forward for Europeans, but also for Americans and others, is to put more sanctions on the Russian regime, not less. So buying Russian energy is a very stupid idea. I can assure you that there is no European leader who is willing to buy Russian gas in the next few years.

“What we want is for Russia to stop this war, and as long as they don’t we will hit them hard in their pockets with sanctions.”

Aid packages

The Dutch government announced on Wednesday it was spending another €1.2 billion on non-military aid to Ukraine over the next three years, as well as €500 million on military support in the form of air defence and drones.

The non-military aid, announced by foreign trade minister Sjoerd Sjoerdsma on a visit to Kyiv, will address “the most urgent needs” such as energy, drinking water, humanitarian aid, healthcare and medicine, as well as operations to clear landmines.

“Russia is hoping to break Ukraine’s morale, its society and its economy,” Jetten said.

“But they will not succeed. Firstly because of the great courage and resilience of the Ukrainians themselves, but also because we as allies realise that we must not let up on giving our support.”

World.title: Booking can compel staff to spend two days in the office: court
World.content:
A court has ruled that travel website Booking.com can compel its staff to spend at least two days a week in the office, settling a dispute with the company’s works council.

The decision was widely expected after the judge remarked at an earlier hearing that requiring employees to spend 40% of their contracted hours on site was “very normal”.

Just over a quarter of Booking.com’s 7,000 staff currently travel to its head office in Amsterdam twice a week. The company had advised its workers to spend two days in the office to promote better workplace relations, training and efficient working practices.

But when bosses tried to make the two-day guideline a mandatory requirement, the works council objected. It said the impact on people’s work-life balance, commuting times and travel costs was too great and questioned whether it would lead to improved performance.

The judge said the company had taken employees’ concerns into account and responded by introducing a six-month transition period and deciding to set the minimum office time at 40% rather than 50% or 60%.

Booking said it welcomed the judgment, pointing out that the two-day rule was not a new measure but a “strengthening of our current policy”.

“We value the relationship with our works council and will continue to hold constructive dialogue with them and our employees as we roll this policy out further,” a spokesman said.

Employment lawyer Pascal Besselink told RTL Nieuws other companies that wanted staff to spend more time in the office would be studying the judgment closely.

“They will always strive to maintain a good relationship with their employees and works council and consult thoroughly on arrangements about home working,” he said.

Two explosives from the Second World War have been discovered at Eindhoven Airport during renovation groundwork next to one of the airport’s runways.

A spokesperson for the Royal Marechaussee, a branch of the military police, said the explosives were found on Wednesday morning on the military side of the airport, which shares the runway with civilian planes, Brabants Dagblad reported.

One of the items is a mortar shell, and the other has not yet been identified, the spokesperson told broadcaster NOS.

No air traffic was disrupted by the discovery and no civilians were at any harm.

World.title: “Strict” Dutch border controls lead to 650 refusals in 21 months
World.content:
Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Fewer than 700 people were turned away at the Dutch border in 21 months of extra border controls that were introduced as part of the “strictest asylum policy ever”.

Border police stopped 43,210 vehicles and checked 182,700 people crossing land borders into Belgium and Germany after the last government reintroduced border controls in December 2024.

A total of 650 people were refused entry while trying to cross the border by road during the period until the checks, introduced by former asylum minister Marjolein Faber of the far-right PVV party, ended in September.

Police arrested 300 people, of whom 40 were suspected of involvement in human trafficking. The government also said 140 people claimed asylum after being stopped at the border.

Some 70% of people stopped at the land borders were EU citizens, asylum minister Bart van den Brink said in a letter to parliament. Border police also checked 398,000 people travelling on flights within the Schengen zone, 85% of whom had EU passports.

Van den Brink said the checks were stepped up to deal with the “significant impact of the continued influx of irregular migration”.

According to Frontex figures, the number of irregular border crossings is down by 26% since 2024. In the same period there has been a 25% drop in first-time asylum applications in the Netherlands.

Schengen zone rules allow member states to reinstate border checks as a temporary measure if there is a threat to security or public order, but they must keep the EU updated on progress.

World.title: Police seize dozens of servers in Limburg over cybercrime
World.content:
The police have seized dozens of servers from a data centre in Limburg that were allegedly used to distribute child pornography, as well as carry out cyberattacks and phishing scams.

The seizures are part of an investigation into an unnamed company, a so-called bulletproof hoster, which provides web space and server access to criminal groups.

Police say they have now gained information on over 3,000 customers who used the servers, and that the hunt for those people is now underway.

At the same time, the FBI and German police also acted against suspects revealed in the investigation, seizing cryptocurrency and shutting down online infrastructure.

The location of the data centre has not yet been made public since the servers in question were housed alongside legal ones, local broadcaster L1 reported.

Police confirmed around 50 servers were taken on Tuesday. The US department of justice announced at the same time that the FBI had taken action against a site called Virtualine, with assistance from Dutch, British and German authorities. The connection between these cases has not yet been confirmed.

The seizure follows a raid in July on the hosting company used by Motherless, a porn website which contained huge amounts of abusive material. NOS later reported that the site’s own employees had uploaded child pornography.

World.title: Free as a bird? New law for freelancers goes into consultation
World.content:
If you work as a freelancer or have your own business, you should be aware of a new law that the Dutch government has just proposed.

The Zelfstandigenwet, or freelance law, aims to create more “peace and clarity” for people who want to work on their own, according to employment minister Thierry Aartsen.

There has already been an exodus of freelancers due to a crackdown on “sham” self-employment, but tax advisers believe people should not panic.

“Don’t get scared,” said an adviser for Blue Umbrella tax service. “Believe in your business, believe in being self-supporting and go for it! Economic growth comes from small and medium-sized enterprises and the government knows that.”

Tests

The new law proposal, which could come into force in 2028 if the minority government manages to find support, will make it clearer what you need to do to be considered a freelancer, or “zzp’er”.

In the past, this group could get a special document from the tax office confirming their freelance status but instead of this formal recognition, there will be a series of tests.

You will need to be registered with the Chamber of Commerce (Kamer van Koophandel) – which is true for most businesses, in any case. You will also need a VAT number and a business bank account, and you must have worked for at least three different clients in two years. Freelancers may also need a specific financial buffer, insurance and pension savings.

Another test will examine how independently you work, including whether you can organise your working hours and take financial risks.

Portfolio

Blue Umbrella recommends making it clear to your potential customers that you will meet the requirements. “Make a portfolio of your clients and what you did in the past year,” the advisor said. “Show that you have a substantial business with multiple clients and you are developing yourself. That gives them trust that they can hire you.”

There is currently an internet consultation running for all freelancers and interested parties until October 29. When the law comes in, however, it may be tested in court: it is not clear why someone with three clients could objectively be called freelance as opposed to someone with two.

Reduction

Under pressure from unions and the European Commission, which has linked some of the compensation for the Netherlands during corona to reducing “fake freelancing”, the number of Dutch self-employed workers has already gone down.

A report last week from the DNB central bank found that there were 131,000 fewer freelancers halfway through 2026 than there were at the end of 2024. The peak came in 2024, when almost 1.3 million people worked for themselves.

According to the report, a third of those who stopped found a permanent job or one that could become a fixed contract. But 40% of the people who stopped freelancing switched to work in a completely different occupation, and 7% became unemployed.

Complex

Blue Umbrella has seen some clients close their businesses too, but stressed that people should not despair: this issue has been around for a long time and, in practice, it is complex. The proposed law aims to help people prove they are genuinely self-employed in future but it would not necessarily stop people who are currently freelancing, under the current rules.

“If you talk about whether someone can make their own decisions as one of the factors to judge whether they are self-employed, it’s a hard question,” said the adviser. “Even as a contractor, you always follow the instructions of the client. You can’t just do your own thing because you think it’s your decision. That would be absurd!”

That said, it’s a good idea to be careful with your finances and consider what extra investments you might want to make, if there are uncertainties in the future of self-employment in the Netherlands.

But do not give up! “The biggest tax revenue comes from small businesses and they are our economic drivers, not the big companies,” he said. “The world will change, and at the end of the day, you have to do it yourself, not rely on the government!”

Find out more about Blue Umbrella’s cost-efficient scheme for businesses and tax services for internationals

World.title: PostNL worker faces 10 years over deadly fake pill webshop
World.content:
The public prosecution service (OM) is demanding prison sentences of 10 and 6.5 years for two suspects accused of involvement in a counterfeit medicine webshop, whose products appear to have led to the deaths of three people.

The pair are alleged to have worked for an organisation that set up dozens of online sites offering prescription pills like sedatives, painkillers and sleeping aids. The sites were shutdown last week and three people arrested for orchestrating the operation.

People bought the pills online without knowing what was actually in them. Some contained powerful synthetic opioids like nitazenes, which can be far more deadly than fentanyl.

The two suspects were not the main players in the case; one is accused of storing and packing the orders, and the other of using his role in the postal service to ensure deliveries were made.

The PostNL employee is also suspected of importing and dealing in large quantities of cocaine, according to broadcaster NOS.

Both suspects say they had no idea they were helping distribute contaminated pills. A lawyer for one of the defendants described his client as a “glorified assembly-line worker”.

World.title: King sees challenges and successes on visit to asylum centre
World.content:
King Willem-Alexander has visited one of the Netherlands’ longest running accommodation centres for asylum seekers to talk to refugees and local residents.

The king received an enthusiastic reception from the 530 people living in the centre in Leersum, Utrecht province, which has been operational for 35 years.

He said he wanted to see how a refugee centre “can be integrated into a local community”, but also gain an insight into the challenges for people living in the area.

During his visit he was shown the facilities in the centre such as a women’s café with yoga and cooking workshops, a bicycle repair shop and support for refugees looking for work or training.

“We all know what the problems are and we see them a lot,” the king said. “But it is also good to be able to show, by being here and bringing lots of journalists along, that things can go very well.”

He was handed a bundle of letters from primary school children, in which they told their personal stories and described how they missed their parents.

The head of the school, Bea, who has been teaching refugee children for 16 years, told AD.nl that the outlook was bleaker than at any time she could remember because of the length of time it is taking for asylum claims to be processed.

“A large group of children are still waiting for their parents, whom they haven’t seen for two or three years in some cases, to be given residency permits,” she said. “We have to deal with that as well as teaching classes.”

World.title: Poland detains Ukrainian accused of arson attack in Romania on behalf of Russia
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Poland has detained a Ukrainian citizen who is wanted by Romania on suspicion of involvement in an arson attack on a defence company carried out on behalf of Russia. On Tuesday, the Polish police’s Central Investigation Bureau (CBŚP) announced that anti-terrorism officers had detained the man, who can be named only as Artem S. under Polish privacy law, in Warsaw under a European Arrest Warrant issued by Romania. In the early hours of 14 September, a fire broke out in the city of Brașov, Romania, in the immediate vicinity of premises belonging to Carfil, a manufacturer of military equipment. Carfil is a subsidiary of ROMARM, a state-owned defence company. On Monday this week, the Romanian Intelligence Service (SRI) said it had determined that the fire had been deliberately caused by a “sabotage network coordinated from Russia”. It added that “several citizens of former Soviet states who reside in the EU” had been involved in the arson attack. The SRI also revealed that the group’s activities were not limited to Romania. “Its coordinators in Russia had assigned it a wide range of targets across the region, including state-owned and private arms manufacturing facilities, as well as sites of military and industrial interest.” In a separate statement, Romania’s Directorate for Investigating Organised Crime and Terrorism (DIICOT) confirmed that the suspects were a Ukrainian, who was at large in Poland, and two Belarusians, who had already been detained in Germany, where they “had been preparing to commit similar acts”. Polish broadcaster RMF reports, based on sources, that Artem S.’s role in the Brașov attack was to identify a target and to arrange payment for those involved. A Polish court will now decide whether the 25-year-old should be extradited to Romania. Poland itself has been a primary target for Russia’s campaign of sabotage and other so-called “hybrid actions” in Europe. Many of those detained and convicted have been Ukrainian and Belarusians, though some Polish citizens have also been implicated. Poland is the "primary focus" of Russia's sabotage campaign in Europe, finds a new report by the International Centre for Counter-Terrorism. Among 151 incidents identified since 2022, 31 of them took place in Poland – more than in any other country https://t.co/QXfSI00FD6 — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) March 3, 2026 In some cases, such operatives are amateurs – so-called “disposable agents” – recruited, coordinated and paid through messaging service Telegram. Some have also been pre-existing criminal groups hired by Russia to carry out such tasks. In August, a drone production plant belonging to private Polish arms company WB Electronics was targeted in an arson attack that Poland has blamed on Russia. The following month, a ground station in Poland used by Starlink, Elon Musk’s satellite internet company, was likewise hit by an arson attack that Poland blamed on Russia. Two Turkish men were later detained in Germany on suspicion of carrying out the attack. World.title: Poland and UK sign Warsaw Defence Plan to “deter Russian threats”
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Poland and the United Kingdom have signed the Warsaw Defence Plan, an agreement to enhance their cooperation on security. The aim, says the British Ministry of Defence, is to “deter Russian threats”. The plan, which follows on from the two countries signing a strategic defence partnership earlier this year, will include joint development and production of defence technologies and military exercises in the Baltic Sea. The UK and Poland share a deep and historical defence partnership. Today, Defence Secretary @WesStreeting signed the Warsaw Defence Plan to bring our two nations’ Armed Forces and industries closer together and help ensure collective security in Europe. 🇬🇧🤝🇵🇱 pic.twitter.com/IP98D1Qs1L — Ministry of Defence 🇬🇧 (@DefenceHQ) October 27, 2026 “Poland is one of the UK’s closest allies – from flying together in the Battle of Britain, to breaking the Enigma code, they have been a vital partner for our defence for nearly a century,” said British defence secretary Wes Streeting on a visit to Warsaw. “The new Warsaw Defence Plan honours this cooperation and sets out how we will continue to work together today, building a stronger Europe in a stronger NATO,” he added. His Polish counterpart, Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz, declared that “the Polish-British alliance has never been as strong as it is now”. Both he and Streeting also emphasised the importance of working together to support Ukraine. Among the aims listed for the plan are collaboration in the development and manufacture of next-generation air-defence missiles, as well as drones and counter-drone technologies. Earlier this year, Poland and the UK, along with Germany, France and Italy, agreed to jointly develop and procure air-defence systems, including missiles and drones. The Warsaw Defence Plan also pledges to “increase defensive maritime activity in the Baltic Sea through exercises and regional coordination, helping British and Polish forces protect vital lines of communication in the sea”. The two countries will also seek to build upon existing cooperation between their defence industries, including Poland’s purchase of CAMM-ER surface-to-air missiles and 100 launchers from MBDA and last year’s strategic partnership on ammunition production between Poland’s PGZ and Britain’s BAE Systems. Poland and the UK have signed a major new defence and security treaty. The agreement includes plans to jointly develop a new air-defence missile, hold large-scale military exercises, and cooperate on countering Russian hybrid attacks https://t.co/cXeYT2u1lw — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) May 27, 2026 This week’s agreement builds upon the Northolt Treaty signed by Poland and the UK in May this year, under which the two countries agreed to cooperate more closely on security. Last year, Poland signed a similar agreement upgrading relations with France. That followed a strategic partnership agreement with Sweden the previous year. In April this year, Poland signed new comprehensive strategic partnership agreements with South Korea and Japan. This year, it has also deepened security ties with Canada and Norway. In November, Poland will host the first military exercises organised by the so-called Coalition of the Willing. Thousands of personnel from the UK, Poland, France and Germany will test operational readiness for a multinational force to secure a potential future Ukraine peace deal. World.title: US chooses Poland to host service facility for Patriot missiles
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. The United States has chosen Poland to host a new centre for servicing and maintaining missiles used in Patriot air defence systems, in a decision described as “historic” by both Washington and Warsaw. It was chosen ahead of bids from four other European countries. The new centre, the first of its kind ot be located outside the US itself, will “dramatically shorten turnaround times and further secure critical supply lines”, said the US Department of War, announcing the decision on Tuesday. Undersecretary of War Michael P. Duffey added that the choice of a country on NATO’s eastern front “sends a clear message [that] the Alliance is united, serious about deterrence, and ready to back our words with action”. Poland Selected to Host Historic PAC-3 Missile Maintenance Facility, Strengthening Allied Burden-Sharing and Transatlantic Security – U.S. Department of War – Release | @DeptofWar https://t.co/2caqADRRx8 — US Embassy Warsaw (@USEmbassyWarsaw) October 27, 2026 The decision was welcomed by Polish leaders, with defence minister Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz saying that it shows “Poland is a trusted ally and holds an extremely important place on the map of global security”. His deputy minister, Magdalena Sobkowiak-Czarnecka, said that Poland was chosen ahead of rival bids from Germany, the Netherlands and Norway to host the facility. However, US ambassador to Poland Thomas Rose indicated that Sweden, not Norway, was the fourth candidate. Kosiniak-Kamysz and Sobkowiak-Czarnecka both pointed to the role President Karol Nawrocki had played in securing the deal. On many issues, the government is in conflict with the opposition-aligned president, but the two sides worked together on the Patriot bid. Historyczna decyzja! Centrum serwisowania pocisków PAC-3 do systemów Patriot powstanie w Polsce! 🇵🇱 O europejską lokalizację tej inwestycji rywalizowały cztery państwa, obok Polski – Niemcy, Holandia i Norwegia. Już na etapie składania wniosków polska oferta została oceniona… pic.twitter.com/wUgFhzlzUk — Magdalena Sobkowiak (@magdasobkowiak) October 27, 2026 Nawrocki, a conservative, is a close ally of his US counterpart, Donald Trump. The Polish president’s national security advisor, Bartosz Grodecki, claimed that it was “thanks to a conversation between” the two presidents that the new Patriot servicing centre was being established in Poland. The head of Nawrocki’s foreign policy office, Marcin Przydacz, meanwhile, thanked Washington for choosing Poland to host the new centre. “The Polish-American alliance and the good atmosphere in relations once again yield results,” he declared. “We can see what positive effects the President’s activity brings for Poland.” Poland is one of a number of European countries that operate Patriot air defence systems. Others include Germany, Greece, the Netherlands, Romania, Sweden and Ukraine. The new centre will service the PAC-3 missiles used in Patriot batteries. The competition to host the facility was announced in July, with the selection made by the US government in conjunction with American defence giant Lockheed Martin, the producer of missiles. In its press release, the Pentagon emphasised that, although Poland would host the new centre, its work would “be underpinned by robust, transatlantic industrial cooperation, with critical supply chain integration led by Germany, the Netherlands and Sweden”. Sweden will deploy Patriot air defence systems and around 100 accompanying military personnel to Poland later this year to protect the NATO logistics hub in the city of Rzeszów, which is the main conduit for aid to Ukraine https://t.co/cq9p7OVO7E — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) October 6, 2026 Global demand for Patriot systems has risen significantly, with the United States expending at least 1,500 interceptors in its war with Iran, according to the Center for Strategic and International Studies. Patriot systems have also been crucial in Ukraine’s defence against Russian ballistic missile attacks, although Ukraine’s supply of missiles is now almost entirely exhausted. After Trump recently suggested that he would authorise Ukraine to produce its own missiles, Poland offered to host any such factory, to ensure its security. However, today’s announcement concerns a site for maintaining and servicing, rather than producing, the missiles. Poland has proposed that, if the United States grants Ukraine permission to produce its own missiles for Patriot air-defence systems, the facility could be located on Polish territory to ensure its security https://t.co/jaQng5wtGg — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) September 28, 2026 The decision cements Poland’s position as one of Washington’s most important security partners in Europe. War secretary Pete Hegseth has praised Poland as a “model ally”, noting that it has for years met NATO’s defence spending targets, unlike many other member states. Poland has also been a significant customer for US defence firms. Between 2021 and 2025, Poland was NATO’s biggest arms importer, with 44% of the equipment it purchased coming from American suppliers. Last year, Poland signed a $2 billion deal for the US to provide logistical support and training for Patriot systems. This year, it was announced that Polish state defence group PGZ would become the first European producer of American Barracuda-500M cruise missiles. Poland will become the first country in Europe to produce cruise missiles developed by US defence firm Anduril Industries The agreement will "transform the continent's defence industry", claims Anduril https://t.co/LPJnwOLfp2 — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 7, 2026 Warsaw is also currently lobbying for a new permanent US military base to be established in Poland, with the government and the president once again putting aside their differences to promote the idea. Last month, Nawrocki claimed that the proposed base, which he said would be called “Fort Trump”, was “confirmed”. However, Washington has not publicly announced any final decision. World.title: Germany’s economy minister hails Poland as “example of great success”
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Germany’s economy minister, Katherina Reiche, has praised Poland as an “example of great success”, saying that it offers a model for other countries. Speaking at the fourth Polish-German Economic Forum in Warsaw, which she opened on Monday alongside Polish finance minister Andrzej Domański, Reiche highlighted the deepening trade ties between the two countries. She noted that bilateral trade last year exceeded €180 billion for the first time, up from €25 billion in 2000, reports Deutsche Welle. Germany has been Poland’s biggest trading partner for decades, although recent data suggest that China, for the first time in history, overtook Germany as Poland’s largest source of imports in July this year. Germany has also long been a major investor in Poland. But Reiche welcomed growing recent investments by Polish companies in Germany, which she said was helping to create jobs. Earlier this year, for example, Poland’s largest manufacturer of trains and trams, Pesa, announced the acquisition of German rival HeiterBlick as part of its efforts to expand its operations across Europe. Reiche noted that around 1,000 Polish companies have invested in Germany, while about 1,600 German companies have invested in Poland, reports Reuters. Poland’s largest manufacturer of trains and trams, Pesa, has announced the acquisition of German rival HeiterBlick as it seeks to expand its operations across Europe https://t.co/N1wE1aYL5m — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) January 12, 2026 Among leading German firms with a presence in Poland are carmakers Mercedes-Benz, which recently invested around €1 billion to build its first electric-only van plant there, which produces its Crafer vans at a plant near the city of Poznań. Reiche also pointed to Poland’s stellar economic performance since joining the European Union in 2004, noting that its GDP has grown by an annual average of 3.8% over that period – twice the EU-wide average. Poland’s economy is on the verge of becoming the 20th largest in the world, with the country hoping to become part of the G20. Meanwhile, Domański used his remarks at the Polish-German Economic Forum to warn Europe against repeating past mistakes as it confronts a rapidly changing geopolitical landscape. He said the continent faced a “unique” historical moment. “The world is changing faster than ever, and we are facing new geopolitical, strategic, and technological challenges.” Europe would need a strong economy and new sources of growth to meet those challenges, he added, warning against what he called “economic naivety” and urging Europe – and Germany in particular – not to return to its previous approach to Russia. “I would like to state this very clearly: Europe must learn from the past. Under no circumstances can there be a return to the previous approach toward Russia. Poland will never agree to that,” Domański said, noting that this position applied in particular to renewed use of Russian energy imports. “We will only be resilient once we are truly independent of external, unstable suppliers of raw materials,” he added, emphasising that Poland and Germany must “work together to modernise the European energy market, focus on technological change and bear security in mind”. Debata ministra @Domanski_Andrz i minister @BMWE_ Katherina Reiche podczas IV Polsko-Niemieckiego Forum Gospodarczego. 💬 Powinniśmy skupić się na cenach energii, ale potrzebne jest znacznie bardziej zdecydowane podejście do ochrony rynku europejskiego. I nie chodzi tu tylko o… pic.twitter.com/NVPUjwx7jA — Ministerstwo Rozwoju i Technologii (@MRiTGOVPL) October 26, 2026 Following the forum, Domański and Reiche attended a meeting of the Friends of Industry, an informal initiative bringing together EU member states to coordinate positions on industrial policy, competitiveness and the operating conditions for European industry. The meeting was attended by representatives of 21 EU member states and European Commission Vice-President Stéphane Séjourné. Discussions focused on protecting and strengthening European industry’s competitiveness and economic security amid geopolitical challenges. “Today, we are facing the consequences of the fact that, in the past, competitiveness was often relegated to second, third or fourth place. Competitiveness took a back seat to other priorities, with the result that European industry now faces serious challenges,” said Domański. He proposed making competitiveness a core EU policy priority, cutting red tape, strengthening the single market, lowering energy costs, investing in strategic technologies such as AI, and tightening trade protections against unfair foreign competition. World.title: Witness testifies Polish president discussed “making money bringing girls” to hotel where they worked 20 years ago
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work!
